You should not take atrovastatin calcium if you have liver disease or cirrhosis.

The breakdown of muscle tissue can lead to kidney failure.
Call your doctor right away if you have unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness.
Do so especially if you also have fever, unusual tiredness, or dark urine.
Serious drug interactions can occur when certain medicines are used together with atrovastatin calcium.
Tell each of your healthcare providers about all medicines you use now, and any medicine you start or stop using.
Avoid drinking more than 1.2 liters of grapefruit juice each day.
Avoid eating foods that are high in fat or cholesterol.
Atrovastatin is often used in conjunction with a cholesterol-lowering diet.

candidates.evidence_text:
When cholesterol and fats build up along your artery walls.
This process is called atherosclerosis.
Cholesterol and fats narrow the blood vessels.
This reduces blood and oxygen flow to your heart, brain, and other parts of your body.
Atorvastatin helps prevent this buildup.
This is done by slowing cholesterol production.
This keeps blood flowing more freely to vital organs.
Lowering your blood level of cholesterol and fats with atorvastatin may help prevent heart disease.
It may also help prevent angina (chest pain).
It may also help prevent strokes.
It may also help prevent heart attacks.
Your healthcare provider will check your blood lipid levels regularly to assess how well your treatment is working.
These measurements include:
LDL-C: Low-density lipoprotein (“bad” cholesterol)
HDL-C: High-density lipoprotein (“good” cholesterol)
TG: Triglycerides (a type of blood fat)
Total-C: Total cholesterol

candidates.evidence_text:
Atorvastatin FDA-approved uses:
To reduce the risk of cardiovascular events in adults with:
Multiple risk factors for coronary heart disease (CHD), but without established CHD.
Use: to reduce the risk of myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, revascularization procedures, and angina.
Type 2 diabetes and multiple risk factors for CHD, without established CHD Use: to help reduce the risk of MI and stroke.
Adults with clinically evident CHD should use this to reduce the risk of non-fatal MI.
It is used to reduce the risk of fatal and non-fatal stroke.
It is used to reduce the risk of revascularization procedures.
It is used to reduce the risk of hospitalization for congestive heart failure.
It is used to reduce the risk of angina.
As an adjunct to diet to lower LDL-C:
Adults with primary hyperlipidemia.
Adults and pediatric patients (10 years and older) with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH).
As an adjunct to other LDL-lowering therapies:
For adults and pediatric patients (10 years and older) with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia.

muscle pain or weakness;
diabetes;
stroke;
a thyroid disorder;
a habit of drinking more than 2 alcoholic beverages per day; or
kidney disease.

This happens more often in women.
This happens more often in older adults.
This happens more often in people who have kidney disease.
This happens more often in people who have poorly controlled hypothyroidism.
Pregnancy:
Tell your healthcare professional if you are pregnant, or plan to become pregnant, or become pregnant.
Atorvastatin may harm your unborn baby.
If you become pregnant, stop taking atorvastatin and call your healthcare provider right away.
Breastfeeding:
Tell your healthcare professional if you are breastfeeding or plan to breastfeed.

Tell each of your healthcare providers about all medicines you use now, and any medicine you start or stop using.

Avoid eating foods that are high in fat or cholesterol.

gt.section_title: What other drugs will affect atorvastatin?

candidates.subject: Atorvastatin
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug has a drug interaction with the drug or substance specified by the object entity that may change effects or cause harm.
candidates.evidence_text:
Sometimes it is not safe to use certain medicines at the same time.
Some drugs can affect your blood levels of other drugs you use.
This can increase the risk of serious muscle problems.
This can make the medicines less effective.
Tell your doctor about all your current medicines.
Many drugs can interact with atorvastatin, especially:
other cholesterol-lowering medicines - gemfibrozil, niacin, fenofibrate, fenofibric acid, and others;
colchicine;
antibiotic or antifungal medicine - rifampin, erythromycin, clarithromycin, itraconazole, ketoconazole, posaconazole, and voriconazole;
birth control pills;
medicine to prevent organ transplant rejection; or
antiviral medicine to treat hepatitis C, HIV, or cytomegalovirus (such as letermovir).
This list is not complete.
Many other drugs may interact with atorvastatin.
List includes prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.
Not all possible drug interactions are listed here.

candidates.evidence_text:
You should not take atorvastatin if you have liver disease or cirrhosis.
Atorvastatin can cause the breakdown of muscle tissue.
The breakdown of muscle tissue can lead to kidney failure.
Call your doctor right away if you have unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness.
Do so especially if you also have fever, unusual tiredness, or dark urine.
Serious drug interactions can occur when certain medicines are used together with atorvastatin.
Tell each of your healthcare providers about all medicines you use now, and any medicine you start or stop using.
Avoid eating foods that are high in fat or cholesterol.
Atorvastatin will not be as effective in lowering your cholesterol.
This is because you do not follow a cholesterol-lowering diet plan.
Atorvastatin is only part of a complete program of treatment that also includes diet, exercise, and weight control.
Follow your diet, medication, and exercise routines very closely.

candidates.evidence_text:
Levothyroxine is a man-made form of thyroxine (T4), one of the hormones your thyroid gland normally produces.
Levothyroxine belongs to a class of medications called hormones.
Levothyroxine works by replacing thyroid hormone that your body is not making enough of.
Levothyroxine is used in adults and children, including newborn babies, to:
treat hypothyroidism (underactive thyroid - a condition where the thyroid gland does not produce enough thyroid hormone).
Levothyroxine replaces the missing hormone whether the condition was present from birth or developed later.
It replaces the missing hormone whether the problem starts in the thyroid gland itself or in the pituitary gland or hypothalamus.
lower the level of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) in the blood in people being treated for a certain type of thyroid cancer, alongside surgery and radioactive iodine therapy.
Levothyroxine injection is used in adults to treat myxedema coma.
Myxedema coma is a rare and life-threatening complication.
Myxedema coma is a complication of a severely underactive thyroid.

Tell your doctor if you have an untreated or uncontrolled adrenal gland disorder or any heart problems such as a recent heart attack.
You will need to start treatment with a steroid (glucocorticoid) medicine.
You will need to start levothyroxine.

Tell your doctor if you develop chest pain, breathlessness, or a fast or irregular heartbeat.

This is more likely after menopause.
Your doctor will aim to give you the lowest dose that controls your thyroid levels.

gt.section_title: What other drugs will affect metformin?
gt.evidence_text: Medicines that have a carbonic anhydrase inhibiting effect like topiramate (often used for seizures or migraines), zonisamide (used for seizures), acetazolamide (used for glaucoma, altitude sickness, and other conditions), and dichlorphenamide (used for a muscle condition called periodic paralysis) can raise the risk of a rare but serious condition called lactic acidosis when taken with metformin. These medicines commonly lower a substance in your blood called bicarbonate, which your body needs to keep its acid levels balanced. If you're taking metformin along with any of these medicines, your doctor may want to monitor you more closely.

candidates.subject: Diabetes Prevention Program (DPP)
candidates.relation_definition: The subject study or trial includes the entity specified by the object as a participant or group.
candidates.evidence_text:
Does metformin work for weight loss?
:
Yes.
Metformin can lead to a modest weight loss.
Results vary.
The weight loss from Metformin is generally smaller than what is seen with medications specifically approved for weight loss.
In the landmark Diabetes Prevention Program (DPP), participants taking metformin lost more weight than those on placebo.
The DPP was a randomized controlled trial in people at high risk for diabetes.
Metformin patients lost 2.7% of body weight after one year.
This was compared to 0.43% for placebo.
Metformin patients also lost 2.1% of body weight after two years.
This was compared to essentially no change (0.02%) for placebo.
29% of people on metformin lost at least 5% of their starting body weight after one year.
Just 13% of people on placebo lost at least 5% of their starting body weight after one year.
This gap held up at the two-year mark.
At the two-year mark, 26% of people on metformin lost at least 5% of their starting body weight.
At the two-year mark, 14% of people on placebo lost at least 5% of their starting body weight.

Boxed warning for lactic acidosis:
Metformin has a boxed warning for lactic acidosis.
Lactic acidosis is a dangerous build-up of lactic acid in your blood.
Lactic acidosis can cause death, hypothermia, hypotension, and resistant bradyarrhythmias.
A boxed warning is the strongest safety-related warning issued by the FDA.
A boxed warning is an extremely rare side effect.
Certain things can raise your risk of lactic acidosis.
Kidney problems can raise your risk of lactic acidosis.
Taking certain other medicines can raise your risk of lactic acidosis.
Being over 65 can raise your risk of lactic acidosis.
Having an imaging test that uses contrast dye can raise your risk of lactic acidosis.
Having surgery or other medical procedures can raise your risk of lactic acidosis.
Conditions that lower oxygen levels in the body can raise your risk of lactic acidosis.
Drinking too much alcohol can raise your risk of lactic acidosis.
Liver problems can raise your risk of lactic acidosis.
Certain rare inherited metabolic disorders (mitochondrial diseases) can raise your risk of lactic acidosis.

candidates.subject: Amlodipine
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the disease or medical condition specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Amlodipine besylate is a prescription medicine.
It is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension).
It is used to prevent certain types of angina (chest pain).
Amlodipine besylate belongs to a class of medications called calcium channel blockers.
Amlodipine besylate works by relaxing and widening the blood vessels.
This causes blood to flow more easily.
This improves blood pressure.
Amlodipine besylate controls angina chest pain by increasing the supply of blood to the heart.
If taken regularly, Amlodipine besylate controls chest pain.
Amlodipine besylate does not stop chest pain once Amlodipine besylate starts.
Your doctor may prescribe a different medication to take when you have chest pain.
Amlodipine is also used alone or in combination with other medicines to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) in adults and children at least 6 years old.
Lowering blood pressure may lower your risk of a stroke or heart attack.
Amlodipine besylate is available as:
Amlodipine 5 mg tablets (Norvasc)
Amlodipine 10 mg tablets (Norvasc)
Amlodipine 2.5 mg tablets (Norvasc)

candidates.evidence_text:
Amlodipine besylate is a prescription medicine.
It is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension).
It is used to prevent certain types of angina (chest pain).
Amlodipine besylate belongs to a class of medications called calcium channel blockers.
Amlodipine besylate works by relaxing and widening the blood vessels.
This causes blood to flow more easily.
This improves blood pressure.
Amlodipine besylate controls angina chest pain by increasing the supply of blood to the heart.
If taken regularly, Amlodipine besylate controls chest pain.
Amlodipine besylate does not stop chest pain once Amlodipine besylate starts.
Your doctor may prescribe a different medication to take when you have chest pain.
Amlodipine is also used alone or in combination with other medicines to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) in adults and children at least 6 years old.
Lowering blood pressure may lower your risk of a stroke or heart attack.
Amlodipine besylate is available as:
Amlodipine 5 mg tablets (Norvasc)
Amlodipine 10 mg tablets (Norvasc)
Amlodipine 2.5 mg tablets (Norvasc)

Amlodipine besylate is a prescription medicine.
It is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension).
It is used to prevent certain types of angina (chest pain).
Amlodipine besylate belongs to a class of medications called calcium channel blockers.
Amlodipine besylate works by relaxing and widening the blood vessels.
This causes blood to flow more easily.
This improves blood pressure.
Amlodipine besylate controls angina chest pain by increasing the supply of blood to the heart.
If taken regularly, Amlodipine besylate controls chest pain.
Amlodipine besylate does not stop chest pain once Amlodipine besylate starts.
Your doctor may prescribe a different medication to take when you have chest pain.
Amlodipine is also used alone or in combination with other medicines to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) in adults and children at least 6 years old.
Lowering blood pressure may lower your risk of a stroke or heart attack.
Amlodipine besylate is available as:
Amlodipine 5 mg tablets (Norvasc)
Amlodipine 10 mg tablets (Norvasc)
Amlodipine 2.5 mg tablets (Norvasc)

The initial dose is 5 mg orally within 24 hours of the onset of acute myocardial infarction.
Subsequent doses are 5 mg orally after 24 hours.
Then, the dose is 10 mg orally after 48 hours.
Maintenance dose: 10 mg orally once a day.
Dosing should continue for at least 6 weeks.
Therapy should be initiated at 2.5 mg.

Therapy should be initiated during the first 3 days after the infarct.
Therapy should be withdrawn.
This occurs if prolonged hypotension happens.
Prolonged hypotension is defined as a systolic blood pressure less than 90 mmHg for more than 1 hour.
Uses: Reduction of mortality in acute myocardial infarction

The maintenance dose is 20 to 40 mg orally once a day.

candidates.subject: Lisinopril
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug may cause the adverse effect or symptom specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Lisinopril can harm your kidneys.
This risk is especially high if you also use certain medicines.
These medicines are for infections, cancer, or osteoporosis.
Tell your doctor about all your other medicines, especially:
a diuretic or "water pill" that may increase blood potassium such as spironolactone, triamterene, or amiloride;
NSAIDs (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs) - aspirin, ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), celecoxib, diclofenac, indomethacin, meloxicam, and others;
insulin or diabetes medications;
medicine to prevent organ transplant rejection such as temsirolimus, sirolimus, or everolimus; or
heart or blood pressure medication
lithium
gold injections.
This list is not complete.
Other drugs may interact with lisinopril.
These include prescription and over-the-counter medicines.
These also include vitamins and herbal products.
Not all possible drug interactions are listed here.

candidates.object: tell your doctor about all your other medicines
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug should be taken or used in the manner specified by the object entity (for example with food or at a fixed time).
candidates.evidence_text:
Lisinopril can harm your kidneys.
This risk is especially high if you also use certain medicines.
These medicines are for infections, cancer, or osteoporosis.
Tell your doctor about all your other medicines, especially:
a diuretic or "water pill" that may increase blood potassium such as spironolactone, triamterene, or amiloride;
NSAIDs (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs) - aspirin, ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), celecoxib, diclofenac, indomethacin, meloxicam, and others;
insulin or diabetes medications;
medicine to prevent organ transplant rejection such as temsirolimus, sirolimus, or everolimus; or
heart or blood pressure medication
lithium
gold injections.
This list is not complete.
Other drugs may interact with lisinopril.
These include prescription and over-the-counter medicines.
These also include vitamins and herbal products.
Not all possible drug interactions are listed here.

candidates.subject: Lisinopril
candidates.object: call your doctor for medical advice about side effects
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug should be taken or used in the manner specified by the object entity (for example with food or at a fixed time).
candidates.evidence_text:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to lisinopril.
Signs of an allergic reaction to lisinopril include severe stomach pain, hives, difficult breathing, and swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat.
Lisinopril may cause serious side effects.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
a light-headed feeling, like you might pass out;
high blood potassium - nausea, weakness, tingly feeling, chest pain, irregular heartbeats, loss of movement;
low white blood cell counts - fever, mouth sores, skin sores, sore throat, cough;
kidney problems - swelling, urinating less, feeling tired or short of breath; or
liver problems - loss of appetite, stomach pain (upper right side), tiredness, itching, dark urine, clay-colored stools, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or eyes).
Common lisinopril side effects may include:
headache, dizziness;
low blood pressure, cough; or
chest pain.
This is not a complete list of side effects and others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may report side effects to FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

candidates.subject: Lisinopril
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug may require changes in dosage based on the condition or factor specified in the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Usual Geriatric Dose for Hypertension:
Initial dose: 2.5 to 5 mg orally once a day.
Maintenance dose: Dosages should be increased at 2.5 mg to 5 mg per day at 1 to 2 week intervals.
Maximum dose: 40 mg orally once a day
Usual Pediatric Dose for Hypertension:
Pediatric patients greater than or equal to 6 years of age were studied.
The initial dose was 0.07 mg/kg orally once a day.
The maximum initial dose is 5 mg once a day.
The maintenance dose should be adjusted according to blood pressure response.
Adjustments should occur at 1 to 2 week intervals.
Maximum dose information is provided.
Doses above 0.61 mg/kg have not been studied in pediatric patients.
Doses greater than 40 mg have not been studied in pediatric patients.
This drug is not recommended in pediatric patients less than 6 years old.
This drug is not recommended in pediatric patients with a glomerular filtration rate less than 30 mL/min.

candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug should be taken or used in the manner specified by the object entity (for example with food or at a fixed time).
candidates.evidence_text:
Take lisinopril exactly as prescribed by your doctor.
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Your doctor may occasionally change your dose..
You may take lisinopril with or without food.
Measure liquid medicine with the supplied measuring device (not a kitchen spoon).
Your blood pressure will need to be checked often.
You may need frequent blood tests.
Tell your doctor if you have a planned surgery.
Call your doctor if you have ongoing vomiting or diarrhea, or if you are sweating more than usual.
You can easily become dehydrated while taking lisinopril.
This can lead to very low blood pressure, an electrolyte imbalance, or kidney failure.
If you have high blood pressure, keep using lisinopril even if you feel well.
High blood pressure often has no symptoms.
Store tightly closed at room temperature, away from moisture and heat.
Do not freeze.

candidates.evidence_text:
You should not use Albuterol if you are allergic to albuterol.
You should not use ProAir RespiClick or ProAir Digihaler if you are allergic to milk proteins.
To make sure albuterol inhalation is safe for you, tell your doctor if you have:
heart disease, high blood pressure, congestive heart failure;
a heart rhythm disorder;
a seizure disorder such as epilepsy;
diabetes;
overactive thyroid; or
low levels of potassium in your blood.
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant.
It is not known whether albuterol will harm an unborn baby.
However, having uncontrolled asthma during pregnancy may increase the risk of premature birth.
It may also increase the risk of low birth weight.
It may also increase the risk of eclampsia.
Eclampsia is dangerously high blood pressure.
Eclampsia can lead to medical problems in both mother and baby.
The benefit of preventing bronchospasm may outweigh any risks to the baby.
If you are pregnant, your name may be listed on a pregnancy registry.
The registry is used to track the effects of albuterol on the baby.

candidates.subject: Albuterol Inhalation
candidates.object: keep using all other medications as prescribed by your doctor
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug should be taken or used in the manner specified by the object entity (for example with food or at a fixed time).
candidates.evidence_text:
It is important to keep albuterol on hand at all times.
Get your prescription refilled before you run out of medicine completely.
Keep using all of your other medications as prescribed by your doctor.
Talk with your doctor if any of your asthma medications do not seem to work as well in treating or preventing attacks.
If albuterol seems like you need to use more of any of your medications in a 24-hour period, talk with your doctor.
An increased need for medication could be an early sign of a serious asthma attack.
Only use albuterol as prescribed by your physician.
An overdose of albuterol can be fatal.
Seek emergency medical attention or call the Poison Help line at 1-800-222-1222.

candidates.subject: Albuterol Inhalation
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition or characteristic specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
You should not use Albuterol if you are allergic to albuterol.
You should not use ProAir RespiClick or ProAir Digihaler if you are allergic to milk proteins.
To make sure albuterol inhalation is safe for you, tell your doctor if you have:
heart disease, high blood pressure, congestive heart failure;
a heart rhythm disorder;
a seizure disorder such as epilepsy;
diabetes;
overactive thyroid; or
low levels of potassium in your blood.
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant.
It is not known whether albuterol will harm an unborn baby.
However, having uncontrolled asthma during pregnancy may increase the risk of premature birth.
It may also increase the risk of low birth weight.
It may also increase the risk of eclampsia.
Eclampsia is dangerously high blood pressure.
Eclampsia can lead to medical problems in both mother and baby.
The benefit of preventing bronchospasm may outweigh any risks to the baby.
If you are pregnant, your name may be listed on a pregnancy registry.
The registry is used to track the effects of albuterol on the baby.

Use albuterol inhalation exactly as prescribed by your doctor.
Follow all directions on your prescription label.

Read all patient information, medication guides, and instruction sheets provided to you.
Ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions.

Your medicine comes with directions for priming if needed.
You may also need to shake your albuterol device just before each use.

Follow all medication instructions very carefully.

To prevent exercise-induced bronchospasm, use 2 inhalations 15 to 30 minutes before you exercise.

gt.evidence_text: Metoprolol is a beta-blocker medication used to treat high blood pressure, chest pain (angina), and heart failure, and to improve survival after a heart attack. It works mainly on the heart, so it is called a cardioselective beta-blocker.

candidates.evidence_text:
Metoprolol is a beta-blocker medication.
Metoprolol is used to treat high blood pressure.
Metoprolol is used to treat chest pain (angina).
Metoprolol is used to treat heart failure.
Metoprolol is used to improve survival after a heart attack.
Metoprolol works mainly on the heart.
Metoprolol is called a cardioselective beta-blocker.
Metoprolol works by blocking the effect of adrenaline and noradrenaline on beta-1 receptors in your heart.
This slows your heart rate.
It reduces how hard your heart squeezes.
It lowers your blood pressure.
Because the heart is doing less work, Metoprolol needs less oxygen.
This is why metoprolol also helps with angina.
Exactly how metoprolol works is not fully understood.
It works for high blood pressure.
It works for heart failure.
It works after a heart attack.
At higher blood levels, metoprolol also blocks beta-2 receptors in the airways and blood vessels.
Metoprolol still needs care in people with breathing problems.
This is because metoprolol blocks beta-2 receptors in the airways and blood vessels at higher blood levels.

Common side effects of metoprolol:
In studies of people taking metoprolol for high blood pressure or angina:
Tiredness and dizziness occurred in about 10% of people
Low mood or depression was reported in about 5 out of 100 people

Itching or rash occurred in about 5% of people
Shortness of breath and a slow heartbeat occurred in about 3% of people

candidates.evidence_text:
Metoprolol is a beta-blocker medication.
Metoprolol is used to treat high blood pressure.
Metoprolol is used to treat chest pain (angina).
Metoprolol is used to treat heart failure.
Metoprolol is used to improve survival after a heart attack.
Metoprolol works mainly on the heart.
Metoprolol is called a cardioselective beta-blocker.
Metoprolol works by blocking the effect of adrenaline and noradrenaline on beta-1 receptors in your heart.
This slows your heart rate.
It reduces how hard your heart squeezes.
It lowers your blood pressure.
Because the heart is doing less work, Metoprolol needs less oxygen.
This is why metoprolol also helps with angina.
Exactly how metoprolol works is not fully understood.
It works for high blood pressure.
It works for heart failure.
It works after a heart attack.
At higher blood levels, metoprolol also blocks beta-2 receptors in the airways and blood vessels.
Metoprolol still needs care in people with breathing problems.
This is because metoprolol blocks beta-2 receptors in the airways and blood vessels at higher blood levels.

Rosuvastatin (Crestor) is a prescription medicine.
The medicine is used to treat high cholesterol.
The medicine is used to reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events.
Major cardiovascular events include heart attack and stroke.
Rosuvastatin belongs to a class of medicines called statins.
Rosuvastatin works by blocking HMG-CoA reductase.
HMG-CoA reductase is the rate-limiting enzyme the liver uses to make cholesterol.
With cholesterol synthesis reduced, the liver increases its LDL receptors.
The liver clears more LDL from the blood.
LDL is "bad" cholesterol.
LDL and total cholesterol levels fall.
The maximum reduction is usually reached by four weeks.
Rosuvastatin comes as a tablet.
Rosuvastatin was first approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on August 12, 2003, under the brand name Crestor.
Many generic versions of rosuvastatin tablets have since been approved.

The medicine is used to treat high cholesterol.
The medicine is used to reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events.

Rosuvastatin comes as a tablet.

Rosuvastatin (Crestor) is a prescription medicine.
The medicine is used to treat high cholesterol.
The medicine is used to reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events.
Major cardiovascular events include heart attack and stroke.
Rosuvastatin belongs to a class of medicines called statins.
Rosuvastatin works by blocking HMG-CoA reductase.
HMG-CoA reductase is the rate-limiting enzyme the liver uses to make cholesterol.
With cholesterol synthesis reduced, the liver increases its LDL receptors.
The liver clears more LDL from the blood.
LDL is "bad" cholesterol.
LDL and total cholesterol levels fall.
The maximum reduction is usually reached by four weeks.
Rosuvastatin comes as a tablet.
Rosuvastatin was first approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on August 12, 2003, under the brand name Crestor.
Many generic versions of rosuvastatin tablets have since been approved.

The most common side effects may include headache, nausea, muscle aches and pains, weakness, and constipation.

Rosuvastatin may cause serious side effects, including:

candidates.evidence_text:
Rosuvastatin (Crestor) is a prescription medicine.
The medicine is used to treat high cholesterol.
The medicine is used to reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events.
Major cardiovascular events include heart attack and stroke.
Rosuvastatin belongs to a class of medicines called statins.
Rosuvastatin works by blocking HMG-CoA reductase.
HMG-CoA reductase is the rate-limiting enzyme the liver uses to make cholesterol.
With cholesterol synthesis reduced, the liver increases its LDL receptors.
The liver clears more LDL from the blood.
LDL is "bad" cholesterol.
LDL and total cholesterol levels fall.
The maximum reduction is usually reached by four weeks.
Rosuvastatin comes as a tablet.
Rosuvastatin was first approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on August 12, 2003, under the brand name Crestor.
Many generic versions of rosuvastatin tablets have since been approved.

gt.section_title: What other drugs will affect rosuvastatin?
gt.evidence_text:
Taking rosuvastatin with certain medicines may increase the risk of muscle problems. Especially tell your doctor if you take:
- cyclosporine (a medicine for your immune system)
- teriflunomide (a medicine used to treat relapsing remitting multiple sclerosis)
- enasidenib (a medicine used to treat acute myeloid leukemia)
- capmatinib (a medicine for the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer)
- fostamatinib (a medicine used to treat low platelet counts)
- febuxostat (a medicine used to treat and prevent high blood levels of uric acid)
- gemfibrozil (a fibric acid medicine for lowering cholesterol)

candidates.subject: Gabapentin
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the disease or medical condition specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Gabapentin works by calming overactive electrical signals in the brain and nervous system.
Gabapentin does this by binding to the alpha-2-delta subunit of calcium channels in nerve cells.
This subunit is thought to normalize chemical signals nerves send to each other.
This results in a calmer, less excitable nerve circuit.
That same effect helps in different ways depending on what gabapentin is treating:
Epilepsy - dampens the runaway electrical firing that causes seizures.
Postherpetic neuralgia (shingles nerve pain) - reduces the abnormal pain signals from nerves damaged by shingles.
Restless legs syndrome (gabapentin enacarbil / Horizant) has an exact mechanism that is less clear.
The same calming effect on overactive nerves is thought to ease the urge-to-move sensation.
Gabapentin is not an opioid, sedative, or anti-inflammatory painkiller.
Gabapentin works directly on the nerves.
Gabapentin helps nerve-related pain.
Gabapentin isn't useful for everyday pain like headaches or sprains.
Most people need 1 to 2 weeks of regular dosing for the full effect to build up.

candidates.evidence_text:
Gabapentin works by calming overactive electrical signals in the brain and nervous system.
Gabapentin does this by binding to the alpha-2-delta subunit of calcium channels in nerve cells.
This subunit is thought to normalize chemical signals nerves send to each other.
This results in a calmer, less excitable nerve circuit.
That same effect helps in different ways depending on what gabapentin is treating:
Epilepsy - dampens the runaway electrical firing that causes seizures.
Postherpetic neuralgia (shingles nerve pain) - reduces the abnormal pain signals from nerves damaged by shingles.
Restless legs syndrome (gabapentin enacarbil / Horizant) has an exact mechanism that is less clear.
The same calming effect on overactive nerves is thought to ease the urge-to-move sensation.
Gabapentin is not an opioid, sedative, or anti-inflammatory painkiller.
Gabapentin works directly on the nerves.
Gabapentin helps nerve-related pain.
Gabapentin isn't useful for everyday pain like headaches or sprains.
Most people need 1 to 2 weeks of regular dosing for the full effect to build up.

candidates.evidence_text:
Gabapentin works by calming overactive electrical signals in the brain and nervous system.
Gabapentin does this by binding to the alpha-2-delta subunit of calcium channels in nerve cells.
This subunit is thought to normalize chemical signals nerves send to each other.
This results in a calmer, less excitable nerve circuit.
That same effect helps in different ways depending on what gabapentin is treating:
Epilepsy - dampens the runaway electrical firing that causes seizures.
Postherpetic neuralgia (shingles nerve pain) - reduces the abnormal pain signals from nerves damaged by shingles.
Restless legs syndrome (gabapentin enacarbil / Horizant) has an exact mechanism that is less clear.
The same calming effect on overactive nerves is thought to ease the urge-to-move sensation.
Gabapentin is not an opioid, sedative, or anti-inflammatory painkiller.
Gabapentin works directly on the nerves.
Gabapentin helps nerve-related pain.
Gabapentin isn't useful for everyday pain like headaches or sprains.
Most people need 1 to 2 weeks of regular dosing for the full effect to build up.

candidates.subject: Gabapentin

candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug produces its therapeutic effect through the biological mechanism specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Gabapentin works by calming overactive electrical signals in the brain and nervous system.
Gabapentin does this by binding to the alpha-2-delta subunit of calcium channels in nerve cells.
This subunit is thought to normalize chemical signals nerves send to each other.
This results in a calmer, less excitable nerve circuit.
That same effect helps in different ways depending on what gabapentin is treating:
Epilepsy - dampens the runaway electrical firing that causes seizures.
Postherpetic neuralgia (shingles nerve pain) - reduces the abnormal pain signals from nerves damaged by shingles.
Restless legs syndrome (gabapentin enacarbil / Horizant) has an exact mechanism that is less clear.
The same calming effect on overactive nerves is thought to ease the urge-to-move sensation.
Gabapentin is not an opioid, sedative, or anti-inflammatory painkiller.
Gabapentin works directly on the nerves.
Gabapentin helps nerve-related pain.
Gabapentin isn't useful for everyday pain like headaches or sprains.
Most people need 1 to 2 weeks of regular dosing for the full effect to build up.

candidates.subject: Gabapentin

candidates.evidence_text:
Gabapentin works by calming overactive electrical signals in the brain and nervous system.
Gabapentin does this by binding to the alpha-2-delta subunit of calcium channels in nerve cells.
This subunit is thought to normalize chemical signals nerves send to each other.
This results in a calmer, less excitable nerve circuit.
That same effect helps in different ways depending on what gabapentin is treating:
Epilepsy - dampens the runaway electrical firing that causes seizures.
Postherpetic neuralgia (shingles nerve pain) - reduces the abnormal pain signals from nerves damaged by shingles.
Restless legs syndrome (gabapentin enacarbil / Horizant) has an exact mechanism that is less clear.
The same calming effect on overactive nerves is thought to ease the urge-to-move sensation.

The initial dose is gabapentin 300 mg orally on day one.
On day two, the dose is 300 mg orally 2 times a day.
On day three, the dose is 300 mg orally 3 times a day.

Doses above 1,800 mg a day did not add benefit in studies.

Maintenance dose: Gralise should be titrated to 1800 mg orally once daily with the evening meal.
Recommended titration schedule:
Day 1: 300 mg orally with the evening meal
Day 2: 600 mg orally with the evening meal
Days 3 through 6: 900 mg orally with the evening meal
Days 7 through 10: 1200 mg orally with the evening meal
Days 11 through 14: 1500 mg orally with the evening meal
Day 15: 1800 mg orally with the evening meal
Notes
Gralise is not interchangeable with other gabapentin products.

gt.evidence_text: Bupropion is an antidepressant medication used to treat depression and seasonal affective disorder. It also supports smoking cessation and weight management. Bupropion is the active ingredient in Wellbutrin and Zyban, Auvelity contains bupropion and dextromethorphan, and Contrave contains bupropion and naltrexone. Bupropion improves mood regulation and nicotine cravings and, when combined with naltrexone, helps reduce food intake.

candidates.subject: Bupropion
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug increases the level of the substance or biomarker specified by the object entity in the body.
candidates.evidence_text:
Examples of CYP2B6 inhibitors include ticlopidine or clopidogrel.
Bupropion inhibits CYP2D6.
Bupropion can increase concentrations of antidepressants.
Examples of antidepressants include venlafaxine, nortriptyline, imipramine, desipramine, paroxetine, fluoxetine, and sertraline.
Bupropion can increase concentrations of antipsychotics.
Examples of antipsychotics include haloperidol, risperidone, and thioridazine.
Bupropion can increase concentrations of beta-blockers.
An example of a beta-blocker is metoprolol.

candidates.evidence_text:
Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic.
It is often called a water pill.
It is used to treat high blood pressure.
It is used to reduce a build-up of fluid in the body.
This build-up of fluid is called edema.
Hydrochlorothiazide works by making the kidneys pass more salt and water out of the body.
You urinate more.
Hydrochlorothiazide is often shortened to HCTZ on prescriptions and medical records.
Hydrochlorothiazide is available as a tablet, capsule, and liquid (suspension) taken by mouth.
It is usually taken once or twice a day.
Hydrochlorothiazide is available as:
oral tablet (12.5 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg)
oral capsule (12.5 mg)
powder for oral suspension (10 mg/mL)
Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) brand names included HydroDIURIL tablets (discontinued).
Esidrix (discontinued) was a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Microzide capsules (discontinued) were a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Now generic tablets and capsules are available.
The brand name of hydrochlorothiazide oral suspension is Inzirqo.

candidates.subject: Hydrochlorothiazide
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is used together with the other treatment or lifestyle measure specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Hydrochlorothiazide is approved to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and fluid retention (edema) in certain patients.
High blood pressure:
HCTZ is used to manage high blood pressure (hypertension).
HCTZ is used on its own.
HCTZ is used alongside other blood pressure medicines.
Lowering blood pressure reduces the risk of fatal and non-fatal cardiovascular events, mainly strokes and heart attacks.
All three forms of hydrochlorothiazide, tablets, capsules and the oral suspension, are approved for high blood pressure in adults.
The oral suspension is also approved for children.
Fluid retention:
Hydrochlorothiazide tablets are used to treat a build-up of fluid (edema) associated with:
congestive heart failure
cirrhosis of the liver
kidney conditions, including nephrotic syndrome, acute glomerulonephritis and chronic kidney failure
treatment with corticosteroid or estrogen medicines
The HCTZ oral suspension is approved for fluid retention.
The fluid retention is associated with congestive heart failure, cirrhosis of the liver, and kidney disease.

candidates.evidence_text:
Your doctor will choose the smallest dose that controls your condition.
Your doctor may adjust the dose over time.
Follow your prescription label and do not change your dose yourself.
HCTZ dose for high blood pressure (adults):
Tablets: The starting dose is hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg once a day.
The dose may be increased to 50 mg a day.
The dose is taken as a single dose or split into two doses.
Doses above 50 mg a day are often associated with a marked drop in blood potassium.
Most people do not need more than 50 mg a day when hydrochlorothiazide is taken alongside other blood pressure medicines
The starting dose is a hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg capsule once a day.
It can be taken on its own or with other blood pressure medicines.
Total daily doses above 50 mg are not recommended.
Capsules are approved for high blood pressure only, not for fluid retention.
HCTZ dose for fluid retention (adults):
Tablets: The usual dose is hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg to 100 mg a day, taken as a single dose or split into two doses.
Many people with fluid retention respond to intermittent treatment.

candidates.evidence_text:
Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic.
It is often called a water pill.
It is used to treat high blood pressure.
It is used to reduce a build-up of fluid in the body.
This build-up of fluid is called edema.
Hydrochlorothiazide works by making the kidneys pass more salt and water out of the body.
You urinate more.
Hydrochlorothiazide is often shortened to HCTZ on prescriptions and medical records.
Hydrochlorothiazide is available as a tablet, capsule, and liquid (suspension) taken by mouth.
It is usually taken once or twice a day.
Hydrochlorothiazide is available as:
oral tablet (12.5 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg)
oral capsule (12.5 mg)
powder for oral suspension (10 mg/mL)
Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) brand names included HydroDIURIL tablets (discontinued).
Esidrix (discontinued) was a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Microzide capsules (discontinued) were a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Now generic tablets and capsules are available.
The brand name of hydrochlorothiazide oral suspension is Inzirqo.

Hydrochlorothiazide is approved to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and fluid retention (edema) in certain patients.
High blood pressure:
HCTZ is used to manage high blood pressure (hypertension).
HCTZ is used on its own.
HCTZ is used alongside other blood pressure medicines.
Lowering blood pressure reduces the risk of fatal and non-fatal cardiovascular events, mainly strokes and heart attacks.
All three forms of hydrochlorothiazide, tablets, capsules and the oral suspension, are approved for high blood pressure in adults.
The oral suspension is also approved for children.

Hydrochlorothiazide tablets are used to treat a build-up of fluid (edema) associated with:
congestive heart failure
cirrhosis of the liver
kidney conditions, including nephrotic syndrome, acute glomerulonephritis and chronic kidney failure
treatment with corticosteroid or estrogen medicines
The HCTZ oral suspension is approved for fluid retention.
The fluid retention is associated with congestive heart failure, cirrhosis of the liver, and kidney disease.

gt.evidence_text: Hydrochlorothiazide works by inhibiting the kidneys from reabsorbing sodium and chloride, so more salt and water leave the body in the urine, which helps reduce excess fluid buildup (edema). Exactly how thiazides lower blood pressure is not fully understood. The early effect is thought to come from a drop in blood volume. With longer-term use, blood volume returns towards normal while the blood vessels themselves offer less resistance to blood flow. Hydrochlorothiazide does not usually change blood pressure that is already normal.

Tell your doctor and pharmacist about all the medicines you take, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.
Medicines that need particular care:
Lithium.
Lithium and diuretics generally should not be taken together.
Hydrochlorothiazide reduces how quickly the kidneys clear lithium.
This reduction carries a high risk of lithium toxicity.
Cholestyramine and colestipol.
These cholesterol-lowering resins bind hydrochlorothiazide in the gut.
They can reduce how much you absorb by up to 85 percent for cholestyramine and 43 percent for colestipol.
The doses need to be separated.
The label advises taking hydrochlorothiazide for the oral suspension.
The label advises taking hydrochlorothiazide at least 4 hours before the resin.
The label advises taking hydrochlorothiazide 4 to 6 hours after the resin.
NSAIDs such as ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), diclofenac, meloxicam, indomethacin, celecoxib and aspirin.
NSAIDs can reduce the fluid-clearing and blood-pressure-lowering effects of hydrochlorothiazide.

candidates.evidence_text:
Fluid and salt imbalance:
Hydrochlorothiazide can lower the levels of potassium, sodium, magnesium and chloride in your blood.
Low potassium (hypokalemia) is the most common of these.
It is more likely at higher doses.
It is more likely during rapid fluid loss.
It is more likely if you have severe cirrhosis.
It is more likely after long-term use.
Your doctor will check your blood before you start and at intervals during treatment.
Contact your doctor if you have any of the following, which can be signs of a fluid or salt imbalance:
dry mouth, thirst, or unusual weakness or tiredness
drowsiness, restlessness or confusion
muscle pain, cramps or muscle fatigue
fast heartbeat
passing much less urine than usual
nausea or vomiting
seizures
Kidney and liver problems:
HCTZ reduces the fluid volume in your body.
This reduction can lead to sudden kidney injury.
The risk is higher if you have chronic kidney disease.
The risk is higher if you have heart failure.
The risk is higher if you are already low on fluid.

HCTZ is used to manage high blood pressure (hypertension).

HCTZ is used alongside other blood pressure medicines.

cirrhosis of the liver

It is often called a water pill.
It is used to treat high blood pressure.
It is used to reduce a build-up of fluid in the body.

Hydrochlorothiazide works by making the kidneys pass more salt and water out of the body.
You urinate more.
Hydrochlorothiazide is often shortened to HCTZ on prescriptions and medical records.
Hydrochlorothiazide is available as a tablet, capsule, and liquid (suspension) taken by mouth.
It is usually taken once or twice a day.

oral capsule (12.5 mg)
powder for oral suspension (10 mg/mL)

Esidrix (discontinued) was a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Microzide capsules (discontinued) were a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Now generic tablets and capsules are available.

candidates.subject: Hydrochlorothiazide
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic.
It is often called a water pill.
It is used to treat high blood pressure.
It is used to reduce a build-up of fluid in the body.
This build-up of fluid is called edema.
Hydrochlorothiazide works by making the kidneys pass more salt and water out of the body.
You urinate more.
Hydrochlorothiazide is often shortened to HCTZ on prescriptions and medical records.
Hydrochlorothiazide is available as a tablet, capsule, and liquid (suspension) taken by mouth.
It is usually taken once or twice a day.
Hydrochlorothiazide is available as:
oral tablet (12.5 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg)
oral capsule (12.5 mg)
powder for oral suspension (10 mg/mL)
Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ) brand names included HydroDIURIL tablets (discontinued).
Esidrix (discontinued) was a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Microzide capsules (discontinued) were a brand name for Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ).
Now generic tablets and capsules are available.
The brand name of hydrochlorothiazide oral suspension is Inzirqo.

candidates.subject: Hydrochlorothiazide
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is typically prescribed at the dose or dosing regimen specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Tell doctor if you have muscle cramps, unusual weakness or tiredness, or an irregular heartbeat.
Should you eat more potassium while taking hydrochlorothiazide?
:
Only if your doctor tells you to.
Low potassium can sometimes be managed with potassium-rich foods.
Low potassium can sometimes be managed with a potassium supplement.
Low potassium can sometimes be managed with a different type of diuretic.
This diuretic holds on to potassium.
Do not start any of these yourself.
Too much potassium can be harmful.
Some people on hydrochlorothiazide do not need extra potassium at all.
Is hydrochlorothiazide 12.5mg enough?
:
For many people Hydrochlorothiazide is.
In published trials comparing the two doses, 12.5 mg kept most of the blood pressure reduction seen with 25 mg.
Low potassium was consistently less common at 12.5 mg.
Starting at 12.5 mg is recommended for adults over 65.
Your doctor will decide the right dose for you.
Your doctor may adjust the dose over time.

candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Hydrochlorothiazide is approved to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and fluid retention (edema) in certain patients.
High blood pressure:
HCTZ is used to manage high blood pressure (hypertension).
HCTZ is used on its own.
HCTZ is used alongside other blood pressure medicines.
Lowering blood pressure reduces the risk of fatal and non-fatal cardiovascular events, mainly strokes and heart attacks.
All three forms of hydrochlorothiazide, tablets, capsules and the oral suspension, are approved for high blood pressure in adults.
The oral suspension is also approved for children.
Fluid retention:
Hydrochlorothiazide tablets are used to treat a build-up of fluid (edema) associated with:
congestive heart failure
cirrhosis of the liver
kidney conditions, including nephrotic syndrome, acute glomerulonephritis and chronic kidney failure
treatment with corticosteroid or estrogen medicines
The HCTZ oral suspension is approved for fluid retention.
The fluid retention is associated with congestive heart failure, cirrhosis of the liver, and kidney disease.

gt.section_title: What other drugs will affect hydrochlorothiazide?
gt.evidence_text: - Lithium. Lithium and diuretics generally should not be taken together. Hydrochlorothiazide reduces how quickly the kidneys clear lithium, which carries a high risk of lithium toxicity.

candidates.subject: Hydrochlorothiazide
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug decreases the level of the substance or biomarker specified by the object entity in the body.
candidates.evidence_text:
Tell your doctor and pharmacist about all the medicines you take, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.
Medicines that need particular care:
Lithium.
Lithium and diuretics generally should not be taken together.
Hydrochlorothiazide reduces how quickly the kidneys clear lithium.
This reduction carries a high risk of lithium toxicity.
Cholestyramine and colestipol.
These cholesterol-lowering resins bind hydrochlorothiazide in the gut.
They can reduce how much you absorb by up to 85 percent for cholestyramine and 43 percent for colestipol.
The doses need to be separated.
The label advises taking hydrochlorothiazide for the oral suspension.
The label advises taking hydrochlorothiazide at least 4 hours before the resin.
The label advises taking hydrochlorothiazide 4 to 6 hours after the resin.
NSAIDs such as ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), diclofenac, meloxicam, indomethacin, celecoxib and aspirin.
NSAIDs can reduce the fluid-clearing and blood-pressure-lowering effects of hydrochlorothiazide.

candidates.subject: Hydrochlorothiazide
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug decreases or lessens the condition or effect specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Fluid and salt imbalance:
Hydrochlorothiazide can lower the levels of potassium, sodium, magnesium and chloride in your blood.
Low potassium (hypokalemia) is the most common of these.
It is more likely at higher doses.
It is more likely during rapid fluid loss.
It is more likely if you have severe cirrhosis.
It is more likely after long-term use.
Your doctor will check your blood before you start and at intervals during treatment.
Contact your doctor if you have any of the following, which can be signs of a fluid or salt imbalance:
dry mouth, thirst, or unusual weakness or tiredness
drowsiness, restlessness or confusion
muscle pain, cramps or muscle fatigue
fast heartbeat
passing much less urine than usual
nausea or vomiting
seizures
Kidney and liver problems:
HCTZ reduces the fluid volume in your body.
This reduction can lead to sudden kidney injury.
The risk is higher if you have chronic kidney disease.
The risk is higher if you have heart failure.
The risk is higher if you are already low on fluid.

Does hydrochlorothiazide cause weight loss?
:
Hydrochlorothiazide is not a weight loss medicine.
Some people see the number on the scales drop in the first days or weeks of treatment.
This is extra fluid leaving the body.
This is not any loss of body fat.
Fluid levels off.
Do not take hydrochlorothiazide to lose weight.
Can you drink alcohol while taking hydrochlorothiazide?
:
Alcohol can make the drop in blood pressure that happens when you stand up worse.
This drop in blood pressure may leave you feeling dizzy or faint.
The same applies to barbiturates and opioid pain medicines.
Tell your doctor how much you drink so doctor can advise you.
Does hydrochlorothiazide lower your potassium?
:
Yes.
Hydrochlorothiazide can lower blood potassium.
This condition is known as hypokalemia.
This effect is more likely at higher doses.
This effect is more likely when fluid is lost quickly.
This effect is more likely if you have severe cirrhosis.
This effect is more likely after taking the medicine for a long time.
Your doctor will check your potassium with blood tests.

Stop taking Hydrochlorothiazide and get medical help immediately if your vision drops suddenly.

candidates.evidence_text:
Tell your doctor about all your medical conditions.
Tell your doctor about all your medications.
Do this before starting fluoxetine (Prozac).
Some medical conditions may interact with fluoxetine.
Some medications may interact with fluoxetine.
Some conditions or medications may affect whether fluoxetine is safe for you.
Tell your doctor if you take any of the following medications or supplements:
Triptans (for migraine)
Antidepressants or mood stabilizers, including SSRIs, SNRIs, tricyclics, MAOIs, lithium, buspirone, or antipsychotics
Amphetamines
Opioid pain medications, including tramadol, fentanyl, meperidine, or methadone
Over-the-counter supplements such as St. John's Wort or tryptophan
Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT)
Many of these combinations can increase the risk of serotonin syndrome.
Serotonin syndrome is a potentially serious condition.
Tell your doctor if you have or have had any of the following:
Liver, kidney, or heart problems
Seizures or epilepsy
Bipolar disorder or mania
Low sodium levels in the blood
A stroke or high blood pressure
Bleeding problems
Pregnancy

Stopped taking an MAOI in the last 2 weeks

Important timing rules with MAOIs and thioridazine:

Wait at least 5 weeks after stopping fluoxetine before starting an MAOI or thioridazine

Common amoxicillin side effects:
Common amoxicillin side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or rash.
These side effects affected more than 1% of patients in clinical trials.
Serious amoxicillin side effects:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin.
Signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin include hives, difficult breathing, and swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction.
Signs of a severe skin reaction include fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, and a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
severe stomach pain or vomiting (which may be signs of a serious intestinal condition); or
diarrhea that is watery or bloody (even if diarrhea occurs months after your last dose).
This is not a complete list of side effects.
Others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may also report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

candidates.evidence_text:
Amoxicillin is a penicillin antibiotic.
Amoxicillin is used to treat bacterial infections.
The infections include tonsillitis, bronchitis, sinusitis, pneumonia, and infections of the ear, nose, throat, skin, or urinary tract.
Amoxicillin clavulanate is a combination of amoxicillin and clavulanate potassium.
The amoxicillin fights bacteria.
The clavulanate potassium helps prevent certain bacteria from becoming resistant to amoxicillin.
Amoxicillin is sometimes used together with another antibiotic called clarithromycin (Biaxin).
This combination is used to treat stomach ulcers.
The ulcers are caused by Helicobacter pylori infection.
This combination is sometimes used with a stomach acid reducer called lansoprazole (Prevacid).
Amoxicillin 500mg and 250mg are available as tablets or capsules and as an oral suspension.
Many brands and forms of amoxicillin are available.
Not all brands are listed on this leaflet.

Do not use Amoxicillin if you are allergic to amoxicillin.
Do not use Amoxicillin if you are allergic to any other penicillin antibiotic.
Examples of other penicillin antibiotics include ampicillin, dicloxacillin, oxacillin, and penicillin.
Other penicillin antibiotics include brands such as Omnipen, Principen, Dycill, Dynapen, Bactocill, Beepen-VK, Ledercillin VK, Pen-V, Pen-Vee K, Pfizerpen, V-Cillin K, and Veetids.
Before using amoxicillin, tell your doctor if you are allergic to cephalosporins.
Examples of cephalosporins include Omnicef, Cefzil, Ceftin, and Keflex.
There are other cephalosporins as well.
Also, tell your doctor if you have asthma.
Tell your doctor if you have liver disease.
Tell your doctor if you have kidney disease.
Tell your doctor if you have a bleeding or blood-clotting disorder.
Tell your doctor if you have mononucleosis (also called "mono").
Tell your doctor if you have any type of allergy.
Amoxicillin can make birth control pills less effective.

candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug may cause the serious or potentially dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity that requires medical attention.
candidates.evidence_text:
Common amoxicillin side effects:
Common amoxicillin side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or rash.
These side effects affected more than 1% of patients in clinical trials.
Serious amoxicillin side effects:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin.
Signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin include hives, difficult breathing, and swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction.
Signs of a severe skin reaction include fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, and a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
severe stomach pain or vomiting (which may be signs of a serious intestinal condition); or
diarrhea that is watery or bloody (even if diarrhea occurs months after your last dose).
This is not a complete list of side effects.
Others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may also report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

Common amoxicillin side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or rash.

Serious amoxicillin side effects:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin.
Signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin include hives, difficult breathing, and swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction.
Signs of a severe skin reaction include fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, and a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
severe stomach pain or vomiting (which may be signs of a serious intestinal condition); or
diarrhea that is watery or bloody (even if diarrhea occurs months after your last dose).
This is not a complete list of side effects.

Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.

Amoxicillin is a penicillin antibiotic.
Amoxicillin is used to treat bacterial infections.
The infections include tonsillitis, bronchitis, sinusitis, pneumonia, and infections of the ear, nose, throat, skin, or urinary tract.
Amoxicillin clavulanate is a combination of amoxicillin and clavulanate potassium.
The amoxicillin fights bacteria.
The clavulanate potassium helps prevent certain bacteria from becoming resistant to amoxicillin.
Amoxicillin is sometimes used together with another antibiotic called clarithromycin (Biaxin).
This combination is used to treat stomach ulcers.
The ulcers are caused by Helicobacter pylori infection.
This combination is sometimes used with a stomach acid reducer called lansoprazole (Prevacid).
Amoxicillin 500mg and 250mg are available as tablets or capsules and as an oral suspension.
Many brands and forms of amoxicillin are available.
Not all brands are listed on this leaflet.

Common amoxicillin side effects:
Common amoxicillin side effects may include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or rash.
These side effects affected more than 1% of patients in clinical trials.
Serious amoxicillin side effects:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin.
Signs of an allergic reaction to amoxicillin include hives, difficult breathing, and swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction.
Signs of a severe skin reaction include fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, and a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
severe stomach pain or vomiting (which may be signs of a serious intestinal condition); or
diarrhea that is watery or bloody (even if diarrhea occurs months after your last dose).
This is not a complete list of side effects.
Others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may also report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

Tell your doctor if you have diabetes.
Tell your doctor if you have herpes simplex virus of your eyes.
Tell your doctor if you have tuberculosis or any other infection.
Tell your doctor if you have sores or ulcers inside your nose.
Tell your doctor if you have recently had injury of or surgery on your nose.

:
Use the medicine as soon as you can.
Skip the missed dose if it is almost time for your next dose.
Do not use two doses at one time.

:

candidates.evidence_text:
Follow your doctor's instructions about tapering your dose.
Storage differs between products.
Store Flonase Allergy Relief and Children's Flonase Allergy Relief between 4°C and 30°C (39°F and 86°F).
Store Flonase Sensimist between 15°C and 30°C (59°F and 86°F), and do not refrigerate or freeze Flonase Sensimist.
Throw the bottle away once you have used the number of sprays stated on the carton, even if there is still liquid in the bottle.
The correct amount of medicine in each spray cannot be assured after the labeled number of sprays has been used.
Bottle sizes vary between products and pack sizes.
They range from 30 to 144 metered sprays.
Dosing information:
Usual Adult Dose for Rhinitis (adults and children 12 years of age and older):
Flonase Allergy Relief Nasal Spray (fluticasone propionate 50 mcg per spray):
Week 1: use 2 sprays in each nostril once daily
Week 2 through 6 months: use 1 or 2 sprays in each nostril once daily, as needed to treat your symptoms
After 6 months of daily use: ask your doctor if you can keep using this medicine

candidates.subject: Tamsulosin
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the disease or medical condition specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Tamsulosin is used to treat the symptoms of an enlarged prostate, also called benign prostatic hyperplasia or BPH.
These symptoms include a weak urine stream.
They include trouble starting to urinate.
They include dribbling.
They include a feeling of not emptying the bladder completely.
They include needing to urinate often or urgently.
They include getting up at night to urinate.
Tamsulosin belongs to a group of medicines called alpha blockers.
Tamsulosin works by blocking alpha-1 receptors in the prostate and bladder neck.
Blocking these receptors relaxes the muscle there.
This improves urine flow and eases BPH symptoms.
Tamsulosin is taken once daily, about half an hour after the same meal each day.
Capsules should be swallowed whole and not crushed, chewed, or opened.
The tamsulosin brand name was Flomax.
Flomax has now been discontinued in the U.S.
Generic tamsulosin is available.
Tamsulosin is not approved to treat high blood pressure.
Tamsulosin is not approved for use in women or children.

candidates.relationship: should be used with caution with
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision when used with the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Tamsulosin is broken down in the body mainly by two liver enzymes, CYP3A4 and CYP2D6.
Medicines that block these enzymes can raise the amount of tamsulosin in your blood.
These medicines can increase the risk of side effects.
These medicines block these enzymes.
Do not take tamsulosin with:
strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as ketoconazole
other alpha blockers, such as alfuzosin, doxazosin, prazosin, silodosin, or terazosin
Use with caution, and tell your doctor if you take:
moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as erythromycin
strong CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as paroxetine, or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as terbinafine
cimetidine
warfarin
medicines for erectile dysfunction or pulmonary arterial hypertension known as PDE5 inhibitors, including avanafil (Stendra), sildenafil (Viagra, Revatio), tadalafil (Adcirca, Cialis), and vardenafil (Levitra).
Taking these with tamsulosin can lower blood pressure enough to cause symptoms.
Some of these cautions matter more at the higher 0.8 mg dose than at 0.4 mg.
Your doctor will decide what is right for you.

strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as ketoconazole
other alpha blockers, such as alfuzosin, doxazosin, prazosin, silodosin, or terazosin
Use with caution, and tell your doctor if you take:
moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as erythromycin
strong CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as paroxetine, or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as terbinafine
cimetidine
warfarin
medicines for erectile dysfunction or pulmonary arterial hypertension known as PDE5 inhibitors, including avanafil (Stendra), sildenafil (Viagra, Revatio), tadalafil (Adcirca, Cialis), and vardenafil (Levitra).
Taking these with tamsulosin can lower blood pressure enough to cause symptoms.
Some of these cautions matter more at the higher 0.8 mg dose than at 0.4 mg.

Do not take tamsulosin if you are allergic to tamsulosin or to any of the ingredients in the capsule.
Do not take tamsulosin with other alpha blockers.
Examples of other alpha blockers include alfuzosin (Uroxatral), doxazosin (Cardura), prazosin (Minipress), silodosin (Rapaflo), and terazosin (Hytrin).
Do not take tamsulosin 0.4 mg with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor such as ketoconazole.
These medicines raise tamsulosin levels in your blood.
Tamsulosin can lower your blood pressure when you stand up.
This may make you feel dizzy or faint.
This is most likely when you first start taking it.
This is most likely when your dose changes.
This is most likely when you start Tamsulosin again after a break.
Get up slowly from sitting or lying down.
Be careful driving or doing anything that needs you to be alert until you know how tamsulosin affects you.
In rare cases, tamsulosin can cause priapism.
These cases probably occur in fewer than 1 in 50,000 patients.
Priapism is a painful erection that lasts a long time.
Priapism is not related to sexual activity.

gt.section_title: What other drugs will affect tamsulosin?
gt.evidence_text: Tamsulosin is broken down in the body mainly by two liver enzymes, CYP3A4 and CYP2D6. Medicines that block these enzymes can raise the amount of tamsulosin in your blood and increase the risk of side effects.

candidates.subject: Tamsulosin
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is metabolized by the enzyme or protein specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Tamsulosin is broken down in the body mainly by two liver enzymes, CYP3A4 and CYP2D6.
Medicines that block these enzymes can raise the amount of tamsulosin in your blood.
These medicines can increase the risk of side effects.
These medicines block these enzymes.
Do not take tamsulosin with:
strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as ketoconazole
other alpha blockers, such as alfuzosin, doxazosin, prazosin, silodosin, or terazosin
Use with caution, and tell your doctor if you take:
moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, such as erythromycin
strong CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as paroxetine, or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors, such as terbinafine
cimetidine
warfarin
medicines for erectile dysfunction or pulmonary arterial hypertension known as PDE5 inhibitors, including avanafil (Stendra), sildenafil (Viagra, Revatio), tadalafil (Adcirca, Cialis), and vardenafil (Levitra).
Taking these with tamsulosin can lower blood pressure enough to cause symptoms.
Some of these cautions matter more at the higher 0.8 mg dose than at 0.4 mg.
Your doctor will decide what is right for you.

candidates.evidence_text:
Tamsulosin is used to treat the symptoms of an enlarged prostate, also called benign prostatic hyperplasia or BPH.
These symptoms include a weak urine stream.
They include trouble starting to urinate.
They include dribbling.
They include a feeling of not emptying the bladder completely.
They include needing to urinate often or urgently.
They include getting up at night to urinate.
Tamsulosin belongs to a group of medicines called alpha blockers.
Tamsulosin works by blocking alpha-1 receptors in the prostate and bladder neck.
Blocking these receptors relaxes the muscle there.
This improves urine flow and eases BPH symptoms.
Tamsulosin is taken once daily, about half an hour after the same meal each day.
Capsules should be swallowed whole and not crushed, chewed, or opened.
The tamsulosin brand name was Flomax.
Flomax has now been discontinued in the U.S.
Generic tamsulosin is available.
Tamsulosin is not approved to treat high blood pressure.
Tamsulosin is not approved for use in women or children.

gt.section_title: What other drugs will affect apixaban?
gt.evidence_text:
Tell your doctor about all your current medicines. Many drugs can affect apixaban, especially:
- a blood thinner or any other medicines to treat or prevent blood clots such as enoxaparin, warfarin, heparin, clopidogrel, dipyridamole, prasugrel, and others;
- an antidepressant; or
- NSAIDs (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs) --aspirin, ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), celecoxib, diclofenac, indomethacin, meloxicam, and others.

It is used to treat type 1 and type 2 diabetes in certain patients.
The treatment aims to improve and maintain blood glucose levels.
Insulin glargine is a man-made form of human insulin.
It is used once daily.
It provides a base level of insulin.

In patients with type 1 diabetes, insulin glargine must be used together with a short-acting insulin.

candidates.subject: Insulin glargine
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug may cause the adverse effect or symptom specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Avoid medication errors by using only the medicine your doctor prescribes.
If you use an injection pen, use only the injection pen that comes with insulin glargine.
Attach a new needle before each use.
Do not transfer the insulin from the pen into a syringe.
Never share an injection pen, even if you changed the needle.
Sharing these devices can pass infections from person to person.
Blood sugar can be affected by stress, illness, surgery, exercise, alcohol use, or skipping meals.
Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) can make you feel very hungry, dizzy, irritable, or shaky.
To quickly treat hypoglycemia, eat or drink hard candy, crackers, raisins, fruit juice, or non-diet soda.
Your doctor may prescribe glucagon injections in case of severe hypoglycemia.
Tell your doctor if you have frequent symptoms of high blood sugar (hyperglycemia), such as increased thirst or urination.
Ask your doctor before changing your medication dosage.
Wear a medical alert tag or carry an ID card to let others know you have diabetes.

gt.section_title: How should I use insulin glargine?
gt.evidence_text: Insulin glargine is injected under the skin, using a syringe or insulin pen, once per day at the same time of day.

candidates.subject: Insulin glargine

candidates.evidence_text:
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Use the medicine exactly as directed.
Ask your doctor or pharmacist if you don't understand how to use an injection.
Prepare an injection only when you are ready to give it.
Do not use it if the medicine looks cloudy, has changed colors, or has particles in it.
Insulin glargine is injected under the skin, using a syringe or insulin pen, once per day at the same time of day.
Insulin can be injected into your upper legs (thighs), upper arms, or stomach area (abdomen).
Do not inject into the same place two times in a row.
Avoid injecting into skin that is damaged, tender, bruised, pitted, thickened, scaly, or has a scar or hard lump.
When treating type 1 diabetes, use your short-acting insulin before meals as directed by your doctor.
Insulin glargine must not be given with an insulin pump or mixed with other insulins.
Do not inject insulin glargine into a vein or a muscle.
Your dose needs may change if you switch to a different brand, strength, or form of this medicine.

Take or administer furosemide exactly as prescribed by your doctor.
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Furosemide oral tablets and liquid are taken by mouth.
Measure liquid medicine with the supplied measuring device, not a kitchen spoon.
Furosemide injection is given in a muscle, under the skin, or in a vein.
A healthcare provider will give you this injection if you are unable to take the medicine by mouth.
Using subcutaneous furosemide at home:
You or your caregiver should be trained before your first dose.
You should read the Instructions for Use that comes with your prescription.
Wash your hands first, and check that the liquid is clear and colorless to slightly yellow.
Do not use liquid if you see particles or if liquid is cloudy or discolored.
Subcutaneous furosemide is given into the abdomen only.
You should use a different spot on the abdomen each time.

The infusion takes about 5 hours.
So, plan to stay somewhere you can relax and reach a bathroom.
Apply the device to a flat, clean, hairless area of the abdomen below the rib cage and above the belt line.
Press the device firmly into place.
Do not remove and reapply it.
Limit your activity while wearing device and avoid bending as much as you can.
Do not exercise or do anything that might knock device off.
Do not get the infusor wet.
Do not bathe, shower, or swim while wearing device.

candidates.evidence_text:
Furosemide is a loop diuretic.
Furosemide is used to treat fluid retention (edema).
It is used in people with congestive heart failure.
It is used in people with liver disease.
It is used in people with a chronic kidney disorder such as nephrotic syndrome.
Furosemide is also used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension).
Furosemide works by increasing the amount of urine the body makes.
This helps reduce swelling and symptoms of fluid retention.
It also helps lower high blood pressure.
Furosemide tablets are sometimes called water pills as they increase how much you urinate.
Furosemide is also known as frusemide in some countries.
Furosemide has been available in the United States since the 1960s.
Furosemide comes as tablets.
Furosemide comes as an oral liquid.
Furosemide comes as an intravenous solution.
Furosemide comes as subcutaneous injections and infusions.
Subcutaneous injections and infusions can be given at home.
Subcutaneous injections and infusions are available under the brand names Furoscix and Lasix ONYU.

candidates.evidence_text:
Common side effects:
Common furosemide side effects may include:
diarrhea, constipation, loss of appetite
numbness or tingling
headache, dizziness
blurred vision
redness, bruising, swelling, or pain where a subcutaneous dose is given.
Serious furosemide side effects:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to furosemide, such as hives, difficult breathing, or swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction, such as fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, or a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.
Furosemide may cause other serious side effects.
Call your doctor at once if you have:
a light-headed feeling, like you might pass out
ringing in your ears, hearing loss
muscle spasms or contractions
pale skin, easy bruising, unusual bleeding
high blood sugar, with increased thirst, increased urination, dry mouth, or fruity breath odor
kidney problems, with swelling, urinating less, feeling tired or short of breath

numbness or tingling
headache, dizziness
blurred vision

muscle spasms or contractions
pale skin, easy bruising, unusual bleeding
high blood sugar, with increased thirst, increased urination, dry mouth, or fruity breath odor
kidney problems, with swelling, urinating less, feeling tired or short of breath

candidates.subject: meloxicam
