candidates.evidence_text:
Meloxicam can increase your risk of a fatal heart attack or stroke.
This risk is especially high if you use Meloxicam long term.
The risk is also higher if you take high doses.
The risk is further increased if you have heart disease.
Even people without heart disease or risk factors could have a stroke or heart attack while taking Meloxicam.
Do not use Meloxicam just before or after heart bypass surgery (coronary artery bypass graft, or CABG).
Avoid taking meloxicam after a recent heart attack, unless your doctor tells you to.
You may have an increased risk of another heart attack if you take Meloxicam after a recent heart attack.
Get emergency medical help if you have chest pain, weakness, shortness of breath, slurred speech, or problems with vision or balance.
Meloxicam may also cause stomach or intestinal bleeding.
This bleeding can be fatal.
These conditions can occur without warning while you are using Meloxicam, especially in older adults.
Call your doctor at once if you have symptoms of stomach bleeding.
Such symptoms include black, bloody, or tarry stools.

candidates.evidence_text:
Meloxicam can increase your risk of a fatal heart attack or stroke.
This risk is especially high if you use Meloxicam long term.
The risk is also higher if you take high doses.
The risk is further increased if you have heart disease.
Even people without heart disease or risk factors could have a stroke or heart attack while taking Meloxicam.
Do not use Meloxicam just before or after heart bypass surgery (coronary artery bypass graft, or CABG).
Avoid taking meloxicam after a recent heart attack, unless your doctor tells you to.
You may have an increased risk of another heart attack if you take Meloxicam after a recent heart attack.
Get emergency medical help if you have chest pain, weakness, shortness of breath, slurred speech, or problems with vision or balance.
Meloxicam may also cause stomach or intestinal bleeding.
This bleeding can be fatal.
These conditions can occur without warning while you are using Meloxicam, especially in older adults.
Call your doctor at once if you have symptoms of stomach bleeding.
Such symptoms include black, bloody, or tarry stools.

candidates.evidence_text:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to meloxicam.
Signs of an allergic reaction to meloxicam include hives, difficult breathing, and swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction.
Signs of a severe skin reaction include fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, and a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of a heart attack or stroke.
These signs include chest pain spreading to your jaw or shoulder.
These signs include sudden numbness or weakness on one side of the body.
These signs include slurred speech.
These signs include leg swelling.
These signs include feeling short of breath.
Meloxicam may cause serious side effects.
Stop using Meloxicam and call your doctor at once if you have:
the first sign of any skin rash, no matter how mild;
shortness of breath (even with mild exertion);
swelling or rapid weight gain;
signs of stomach bleeding - bloody or tarry stools, coughing up blood or vomit that looks like coffee grounds;

candidates.subject: meloxicam
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug may cause the serious or potentially dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity that requires medical attention.
candidates.evidence_text:
Meloxicam can increase your risk of a fatal heart attack or stroke.
This risk is especially high if you use Meloxicam long term.
The risk is also higher if you take high doses.
The risk is further increased if you have heart disease.
Even people without heart disease or risk factors could have a stroke or heart attack while taking Meloxicam.
Do not use Meloxicam just before or after heart bypass surgery (coronary artery bypass graft, or CABG).
Avoid taking meloxicam after a recent heart attack, unless your doctor tells you to.
You may have an increased risk of another heart attack if you take Meloxicam after a recent heart attack.
Get emergency medical help if you have chest pain, weakness, shortness of breath, slurred speech, or problems with vision or balance.
Meloxicam may also cause stomach or intestinal bleeding.
This bleeding can be fatal.
These conditions can occur without warning while you are using Meloxicam, especially in older adults.
Call your doctor at once if you have symptoms of stomach bleeding.
Such symptoms include black, bloody, or tarry stools.

Signs of an allergic reaction to meloxicam include hives, difficult breathing, and swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction.
Signs of a severe skin reaction include fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, and a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of a heart attack or stroke.
These signs include chest pain spreading to your jaw or shoulder.
These signs include sudden numbness or weakness on one side of the body.
These signs include slurred speech.
These signs include leg swelling.
These signs include feeling short of breath.
Meloxicam may cause serious side effects.
Stop using Meloxicam and call your doctor at once if you have:
the first sign of any skin rash, no matter how mild;
shortness of breath (even with mild exertion);
swelling or rapid weight gain;
signs of stomach bleeding - bloody or tarry stools, coughing up blood or vomit that looks like coffee grounds;

candidates.subject: meloxicam
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug may cause the adverse effect or symptom specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Meloxicam can increase your risk of a fatal heart attack or stroke.
This risk is especially high if you use Meloxicam long term.
The risk is also higher if you take high doses.
The risk is further increased if you have heart disease.
Even people without heart disease or risk factors could have a stroke or heart attack while taking Meloxicam.
Do not use Meloxicam just before or after heart bypass surgery (coronary artery bypass graft, or CABG).
Avoid taking meloxicam after a recent heart attack, unless your doctor tells you to.
You may have an increased risk of another heart attack if you take Meloxicam after a recent heart attack.
Get emergency medical help if you have chest pain, weakness, shortness of breath, slurred speech, or problems with vision or balance.
Meloxicam may also cause stomach or intestinal bleeding.
This bleeding can be fatal.
These conditions can occur without warning while you are using Meloxicam, especially in older adults.
Call your doctor at once if you have symptoms of stomach bleeding.
Such symptoms include black, bloody, or tarry stools.

The medicine is used when other pain treatments do not treat your pain well enough.

Hydrocodone and acetaminophen first gained FDA approval on May 3, 1982.

Call your healthcare provider if you have any of these symptoms and symptoms are severe.
Get emergency medical help if you have:
Trouble breathing
Shortness of breath
Fast heartbeat
Chest pain
Swelling of your face, tongue, or throat
Extreme drowsiness
Light-headedness when changing positions
Feeling faint
Agitation
High body temperature
Trouble walking
Stiff muscles
Mental changes such as confusion.
These are not all the possible side effects of hydrocodone and acetaminophen.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.
You may report side effects to the FDA at 1-800-FDA-1088.

It can cause low blood pressure.

It can cause unusual snoring.

Your doctor may recommend that you keep naloxone with you at all times.

candidates.evidence_text:
SURPASS-CVOT randomized 13,299 adults with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease.
The adults were randomized to Mounjaro (tirzepatide, up to 15 mg once weekly) or dulaglutide 1.5 mg once weekly.
Dulaglutide is a GLP-1 medicine already approved to reduce cardiovascular risk.
The study had a median follow-up of about 4 years.
Cardiovascular death, non-fatal heart attack, or non-fatal stroke occurred in 12.1% of those taking Mounjaro.
These events occurred in 13.0% of those taking dulaglutide.
The hazard ratio was 0.92 with a 95% CI of 0.83–1.01.
The results met the trial's goal of non-inferiority.
The results did not demonstrate superiority.
Death from any cause occurred in 8.5% of the Mounjaro group.
Death from any cause occurred in 10.1% of the dulaglutide group.
The hazard ratio was 0.84.
The 95% confidence interval was 0.75–0.94.
This outcome was not a primary endpoint.
This outcome was not adjusted for multiple comparisons.
Therefore, Mounjaro results should be read as exploratory.
The comparator was an active medicine rather than placebo.

candidates.evidence_text:
SURPASS-CVOT randomized 13,299 adults with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease.
The adults were randomized to Mounjaro (tirzepatide, up to 15 mg once weekly) or dulaglutide 1.5 mg once weekly.
Dulaglutide is a GLP-1 medicine already approved to reduce cardiovascular risk.
The study had a median follow-up of about 4 years.
Cardiovascular death, non-fatal heart attack, or non-fatal stroke occurred in 12.1% of those taking Mounjaro.
These events occurred in 13.0% of those taking dulaglutide.
The hazard ratio was 0.92 with a 95% CI of 0.83–1.01.
The results met the trial's goal of non-inferiority.
The results did not demonstrate superiority.
Death from any cause occurred in 8.5% of the Mounjaro group.
Death from any cause occurred in 10.1% of the dulaglutide group.
The hazard ratio was 0.84.
The 95% confidence interval was 0.75–0.94.
This outcome was not a primary endpoint.
This outcome was not adjusted for multiple comparisons.
Therefore, Mounjaro results should be read as exploratory.
The comparator was an active medicine rather than placebo.

Common Side Effects:
The most common tirzepatide side effects are:
Diarrhea
Vomiting
Constipation
Nausea (mild to moderate)
Decreased appetite
Abdominal pain.
Serious side effects:
Tirzepatide can cause serious side effects.
Call your doctor right away if you have any of the following:
Stop taking tirzepatide and call your healthcare provider immediately if you have severe pain in your stomach area that will not go away.
This applies if the pain occurs with or without vomiting.
This also applies if the pain spreads to your back.
Severe stomach pain is a sign of pancreatitis.
Diarrhea, nausea, and vomiting can cause dehydration.
Dehydration may lead to kidney problems.
Drink plenty of fluids to reduce this risk.
Tell your doctor if you are unable to keep fluids down.
Gallbladder problems include severe upper stomach pain.
They include fever.
They include nausea.
They include vomiting.
They include yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice).
They include clay-colored stools.
Serious allergic reactions require seeking emergency medical attention.

Do not mix insulin and tirzepatide together in the same injection.
You may give an injection of tirzepatide and insulin in the same body area, but not right next to each other.
Your doctor will probably start you on a low dose.
This dose may be gradually increased.
However, it will not be increased more than once every 4 weeks.
You may change the day of the week you use tirzepatide as long as there are at least three days between doses.
Do not stop taking Tirzepatide without talking to your doctor.
Tirzepatide KwikPen:
The KwikPen contains 4 fixed doses.
One dose is injected weekly (subcutaneously).
For your weekly dose, you need to turn the dose knob all the way until KwikPen stops.
You also need to turn the dose knob until the 1 icon is in the dose window.
After 4 doses, throw away (discard) the Pen, including the unused medicine.

The most common tirzepatide side effects are:
Diarrhea
Vomiting
Constipation
Nausea (mild to moderate)
Decreased appetite
Abdominal pain.
Serious side effects:
Tirzepatide can cause serious side effects.
Call your doctor right away if you have any of the following:
Stop taking tirzepatide and call your healthcare provider immediately if you have severe pain in your stomach area that will not go away.
This applies if the pain occurs with or without vomiting.
This also applies if the pain spreads to your back.
Severe stomach pain is a sign of pancreatitis.
Diarrhea, nausea, and vomiting can cause dehydration.
Dehydration may lead to kidney problems.
Drink plenty of fluids to reduce this risk.
Tell your doctor if you are unable to keep fluids down.
Gallbladder problems include severe upper stomach pain.
They include fever.
They include nausea.
They include vomiting.
They include yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice).
They include clay-colored stools.
Serious allergic reactions require seeking emergency medical attention.

Tell your doctor and pharmacist what prescription and over-the-counter medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are planning to take or are taking.
They may interact with tirzepatide.
Your doctor may need to change the doses of your medications or monitor you carefully for side effects.
Birth control pills may not work as well while receiving Tirzepatide.
Your doctor may suggest you use another form of birth control for 4 weeks after starting tirzepatide.
Your doctor may suggest you use another form of birth control for 4 weeks after each dose change.
Taking tirzepatide with other medicines to treat diabetes, such as sulfonylureas or insulin, may increase your risk of hypoglycemia.
Talk to your doctor and pharmacist about low blood sugar and how to manage low blood sugar.
Tirzepatide delays gastric emptying.
It may alter the absorption of other orally administered medicines.
This list is not complete.
Many other drugs may interact with Mounjaro and Zepbound.
These drugs include prescription and over-the-counter medicines.

There is a list of ingredients in tirzepatide, at the bottom of this page.
Tell your healthcare team if you are planning surgery or other procedure that uses anesthesia or deep sedation.
Tell your doctor if you have or have ever had kidney or pancreas disease, a history of diabetic retinopathy or any stomach problems such as difficulty digesting food.
Tell your doctor if you plan to become pregnant, are pregnant, or are breastfeeding.
If you become pregnant while taking tirzepatide, you should tell your doctor.
There is a pregnancy exposure registry for women who take Zepbound during pregnancy.
Talk to your healthcare provider about how you can take part.
Call 1-844-524-0039.
Visit https://pregnancyregistry.lilly.com/zepbound.

candidates.subject: Tirzepatide
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is typically prescribed at the dose or dosing regimen specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Usual Zepbound Dose for Weight Loss and OSA (Adult):
Initial dose: 2.5 mg under the skin (subcutaneously) once a week.
After 4 weeks: The dosage should be increased to 5 mg subcutaneously once a week.
Further dose increases may occur after at least 4 weeks on the current dose.
The dosage may be increased in 2.5 mg increments.
Recommended maintenance dose for weight loss: 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg injected subcutaneously once weekly.
Recommended maintenance dose for OSA: 10 mg or 15 mg injected subcutaneously once weekly.
Maximum dose: 15 mg subcutaneously once a week.
Dose of Mounjaro for Type 2 Diabetes (Adults and Children 10 Years and Older):
Initial dose: 2.5 mg subcutaneously once a week.
Additional glycemic control is needed.
Increase the dose in 2.5 mg increments after at least 4 weeks on the current dose.
Maximum dose (adults): 15 mg subcutaneously once a week.
Maximum dose (children 10 years and older): 10 mg subcutaneously once a week.
Comments: The starting dose and escalation schedule are designed to reduce the risk of gastrointestinal side effects.

candidates.subject: Tirzepatide
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is typically prescribed at the dose or dosing regimen specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Usual Zepbound Dose for Weight Loss and OSA (Adult):
Initial dose: 2.5 mg under the skin (subcutaneously) once a week.
After 4 weeks: The dosage should be increased to 5 mg subcutaneously once a week.
Further dose increases may occur after at least 4 weeks on the current dose.
The dosage may be increased in 2.5 mg increments.
Recommended maintenance dose for weight loss: 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg injected subcutaneously once weekly.
Recommended maintenance dose for OSA: 10 mg or 15 mg injected subcutaneously once weekly.
Maximum dose: 15 mg subcutaneously once a week.
Dose of Mounjaro for Type 2 Diabetes (Adults and Children 10 Years and Older):
Initial dose: 2.5 mg subcutaneously once a week.
Additional glycemic control is needed.
Increase the dose in 2.5 mg increments after at least 4 weeks on the current dose.
Maximum dose (adults): 15 mg subcutaneously once a week.
Maximum dose (children 10 years and older): 10 mg subcutaneously once a week.
Comments: The starting dose and escalation schedule are designed to reduce the risk of gastrointestinal side effects.

gt.evidence_text: - Maximum dose (adults): 15 mg subcutaneously once a week.

Vomiting
Constipation
Nausea (mild to moderate)
Decreased appetite
Abdominal pain.
Serious side effects:
Tirzepatide can cause serious side effects.
Call your doctor right away if you have any of the following:

They include nausea.
They include vomiting.
They include yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice).
They include clay-colored stools.
Serious allergic reactions require seeking emergency medical attention.

Duloxetine is a selective serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor antidepressant (SSNRI).
Duloxetine affects chemicals in the brain that may be unbalanced in people with depression.
Duloxetine is used to treat major depressive disorder in adults.
Duloxetine is also used to treat general anxiety disorder in adults and children who are at least 7 years old.
Duloxetine is also used in adults to treat nerve pain caused by diabetes (diabetic neuropathy).
It is also used to treat chronic muscle or joint pain (such as low back pain and osteoarthritis pain).
Some brands of duloxetine are also used to treat fibromyalgia (a chronic pain disorder).
Drizalma is for treating fibromyalgia only in adults.
Cymbalta may be used to treat fibromyalgia in adults and children at least 13 years old.

candidates.evidence_text:
Duloxetine is a selective serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor antidepressant (SSNRI).
Duloxetine affects chemicals in the brain that may be unbalanced in people with depression.
Duloxetine is used to treat major depressive disorder in adults.
Duloxetine is also used to treat general anxiety disorder in adults and children who are at least 7 years old.
Duloxetine is also used in adults to treat nerve pain caused by diabetes (diabetic neuropathy).
It is also used to treat chronic muscle or joint pain (such as low back pain and osteoarthritis pain).
Some brands of duloxetine are also used to treat fibromyalgia (a chronic pain disorder).
Drizalma is for treating fibromyalgia only in adults.
Cymbalta may be used to treat fibromyalgia in adults and children at least 13 years old.

dry mouth; or

Beta-blockers affect the heart and circulation (blood flow through arteries and veins).
Carvedilol is used to treat heart failure and hypertension (high blood pressure).
Carvedilol is also used after a heart attack that has caused your heart not to pump as well.
Carvedilol may also be used for purposes not listed in this medication guide.
Carvedilol is not approved for use by anyone younger than 18 years of age.

You should not take carvedilol if you have severe liver disease.
You should not take carvedilol if you have severe heart failure requiring certain IV medications.
You should not take carvedilol if you have a serious heart condition such as heart block, "sick sinus syndrome," or slow heart rate.
You may take carvedilol if you have a serious heart condition such as heart block, "sick sinus syndrome," or slow heart rate and have a pacemaker.
Avoid drinking alcohol within 2 hours before or after taking extended-release carvedilol (Coreg CR).

If you are being treated for high blood pressure, keep using carvedilol even if you feel well.
High blood pressure often has no symptoms.
You may need to use blood pressure medication for the rest of your life.

a seizure;

headache;
dizziness; or
constipation or diarrhea.
This is not a complete list of side effects and others may occur.
Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.

Use famotidine exactly as directed on the label, or as prescribed by your doctor.
Famotidine oral is taken by mouth.
Famotidine injection is given as an infusion into a vein.
A healthcare provider will give you Famotidine if you are unable to take the medicine by mouth.
You may take famotidine oral with or without food.
Shake the bottle of Pepcid suspension (liquid) vigorously for 5 to 10 seconds prior to each use.
Measure the liquid medicine carefully.
Use the dosing syringe provided, or use a medicine dose-measuring device (not a kitchen spoon).
Most ulcers heal within 4 weeks of treatment.
Ulcers may take up to 8 weeks of using this medicine before your ulcer heals.
Keep using the medication as directed.
Call your doctor if the condition you are treating with this medicine does not improve, or if condition gets worse while using this medicine.
Famotidine may be only part of a complete program of treatment that also includes changes in diet or lifestyle habits.
Follow all instructions of your doctor or dietitian.
Store at room temperature away from moisture, heat, and light.

candidates.evidence_text:

Signs of an allergic reaction to famotidine also include difficult breathing.
Signs of an allergic reaction to famotidine also include swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat.
Stop using Famotidine and call your doctor at once if you have:
confusion, hallucinations, agitation, lack of energy;
a seizure;
fast or pounding heartbeats, sudden dizziness (like you might pass out).
Some side effects may be more likely in older adults and in people who have severe kidney disease.
Common famotidine side effects may include:
headache;

constipation or diarrhea.

Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.

kidney disease;
liver disease;
cancer stomach; or

heart disease, high blood pressure, high cholesterol, diabetes, or if you smoke;
a heart attack, stroke, or blood clot;
stomach ulcers or bleeding;

Tell your doctor if you are having trouble getting pregnant.

Take venlafaxine as prescribed by your doctor.
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Your doctor may occasionally change your dose.
Take with food at the same time each day.
Swallow the extended-release capsule or tablet whole.
Do not crush, chew, break, or open it.
If you cannot swallow a capsule whole, open it and mix the medicine with applesauce.
Swallow the mixture right away without chewing.
Tell your doctor if you have any changes in sexual function.
Such changes include loss of interest in sex.
Such changes include trouble having an orgasm.
Such changes include problems with erections or ejaculation in men.
Some sexual problems can be treated.
Your symptoms may not improve for up to several weeks.
Do not stop using venlafaxine suddenly.
You could have severe and long-lasting unpleasant symptoms.
These symptoms include agitation, confusion, tingling or electric shock feelings, aggression, violent behavior, suicidal thoughts, vision changes, or increased blood pressure.

candidates.subject: tramadol
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological or therapeutic drug class specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Tramadol is an opioid agonist.
Tramadol may be used to treat moderate to moderately severe chronic pain in adults.
It is used when other pain treatments such as non-opioid pain medicines do not treat your pain well enough.
It is also used when you cannot tolerate other pain treatments.
Extended-release forms of tramadol may be used in adults who require around-the-clock treatment of their pain for an extended period.
An opioid pain medicine such as tramadol can put you at risk for overdose and death.
You are at risk for opioid addiction, abuse, and misuse that can lead to death.
This risk exists even if you take your dose correctly as prescribed.
Brands of tramadol include ConZip, Qdolo, Ryzolt, Ultram, Ultram ER, and Ultracet.
Many have been discontinued.
Generic tramadol is still available.
Taking tramadol in combination with other pain-relieving medicines can provide better pain relief.
The other pain-relieving medicines include acetaminophen, ibuprofen, or aspirin.
Taking just one pain-relieving medicine by itself provides less relief.

candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug carries a safety warning or precaution about the risk or situation specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
You may have breathing problems or withdrawal symptoms if you start or stop taking certain other medicines.
Tramadol is broken down by two liver enzymes called CYP3A4 and CYP2D6.
Medicines that block or speed up these enzymes change how much tramadol and how much of tramadol's active form are in your body.
Starting one of these medicines and stopping one both shift the balance.
Tell your doctor whenever you begin or finish a course of an antibiotic, antifungal medication, heart or blood pressure medication, seizure medication, or medicine to treat HIV or hepatitis C.
Many other drugs can be dangerous when used with tramadol.
Tell your doctor if you also use:
medicine for allergies, asthma, blood pressure, motion sickness, irritable bowel, or overactive bladder
other opioid medicines
buprenorphine, butorphanol, nalbuphine, or pentazocine.
These opioids work differently.
These opioids can block tramadol's pain-relieving effect.
These opioids can bring on sudden withdrawal symptoms.
Opioids are generally not taken with tramadol.
a benzodiazepine sedative like Valium, Klonopin, or Xanax

are allergic to tramadol, to any of the other ingredients in your product, or to other opioids
have significant breathing problems (respiratory depression)
have acute or severe asthma and are somewhere you cannot be monitored, or where resuscitation equipment is not available
have a known or suspected blockage of the stomach or intestines, including paralytic ileus
have taken a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI) in the past 14 days (such as isocarboxazid, linezolid, methylene blue injection, phenelzine, or tranylcypromine)
are younger than 12 years of age
are younger than 18 years of age and have recently had surgery to remove your tonsils or adenoids.
Seizures have occurred in some people taking tramadol.
Your seizure risk may be higher if you have ever had:
a head injury, epilepsy, or other seizure disorder
drug or alcohol addiction or
a metabolic disorder.
To make sure tramadol is safe for you, tell your doctor if you have a history of:
Head injury or seizures
Problems urinating
Liver, kidney, or thyroid problems

candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the disease or medical condition specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Potassium is a mineral.
Potassium is found in many foods.
Potassium is needed for several functions of your body.
These functions include the beating of your heart.
Potassium chloride is used to prevent or to treat low blood levels of potassium (hypokalemia).
Potassium levels can be low as a result of a disease.
Potassium levels can be low from taking certain medicines.
Potassium levels can be low after a prolonged illness with diarrhea or vomiting.

candidates.subject: Potassium Chloride
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition or characteristic specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
You should not use potassium chloride if you have high levels of potassium in your blood (hyperkalemia).
You should not use potassium chloride if you also take a "potassium-sparing" diuretic.
To be sure potassium chloride is helping your condition.
Your blood may need to be tested often.
Your heart rate may also be checked.
The heart rate can be checked using an electrocardiograph or ECG.
An electrocardiograph or ECG is sometimes called an EKG.
The device is used to measure electrical activity of the heart.
This test will help your doctor determine how long to treat you with potassium.
Do not miss any scheduled appointments.
Serious side effects of potassium include uneven heartbeat.
They include muscle weakness or limp feeling.
They include severe stomach pain.
They include numbness or tingling in your hands, feet, or mouth.
Do not stop taking this medicine without first talking to your doctor.
If you stop taking this medicine suddenly, your condition may become worse.
Do not crush, chew, or suck on an extended-release tablet or capsule.

candidates.subject: Hydroxyzine
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological or therapeutic drug class specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Hydroxyzine is a prescription antihistamine.
It is used to treat anxiety and tension.
It is used to treat itching from allergic skin conditions.
It is used for sedation before and after general anesthesia.
Hydroxyzine comes in three oral forms:
Hydroxyzine hydrochloride (HCl) tablets in 10 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg strengths
Hydroxyzine hydrochloride oral solution (a syrup) containing 10 mg in each 5 mL
Hydroxyzine pamoate capsules in 25 mg
There is also a hydroxyzine hydrochloride injection.
Hydroxyzine is given into a muscle by a healthcare professional.
It is never given into a vein or under the skin.
Hydroxyzine is not chemically related to benzodiazepines, phenothiazines, reserpine, or meprobamate.

candidates.subject: Hydroxyzine
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological or therapeutic drug class specified by the object entity.

candidates.subject: Hydroxyzine
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug produces its therapeutic effect through the biological mechanism specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Hydroxyzine is thought to work by quieting activity in certain deeper regions of the brain.
These regions are located below the outer layer known as the cortex.
Hydroxyzine is not a cortical depressant.
This means Hydroxyzine does not work by slowing down the outer layer of the brain.
Some other sedatives work by slowing down the outer layer of the brain.
Hydroxyzine also blocks histamine, a chemical your body releases during an allergic reaction.
Blocks histamine is what relieves itching.
Laboratory and clinical studies have also shown that hydroxyzine relaxes skeletal muscle.
Hydroxyzine widens the airways (bronchodilation).
Hydroxyzine reduces pain.
These are effects that have been observed rather than uses Hydroxyzine is approved for.
Hydroxyzine has also been shown to reduce nausea and vomiting.
Reduce nausea and vomiting is an approved use for the injection, but not for the forms taken by mouth.

candidates.evidence_text:
Hydroxyzine taken by mouth is approved for three uses.
Three uses are the same for hydroxyzine HCl and hydroxyzine pamoate.
Anxiety and tension.
For symptomatic relief of anxiety and tension linked to psychoneurosis, and as an add-on treatment in physical illnesses where anxiety is present.
Itching from allergic skin conditions.
For managing itching (pruritus) caused by allergic conditions such as long-term hives (chronic urticaria), eczema-type rashes, and rashes caused by contact with an irritant.
Hydroxyzine is also used for itching caused by histamine release.
Sedation around surgery.
As a sedative given before a procedure (premedication) and after general anesthesia.
The injection is also approved for nausea and vomiting.
It is usually given in hospital or clinic settings.
Hydroxyzine should not be used for nausea and vomiting caused by pregnancy.
Hydroxyzine has not been studied for long-term use in anxiety.
Studies have not assessed whether Hydroxyzine still works as an anti-anxiety medicine.
The assessment period is beyond four months.

It is used for sedation before and after general anesthesia.
Hydroxyzine comes in three oral forms:
Hydroxyzine hydrochloride (HCl) tablets in 10 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg strengths
Hydroxyzine hydrochloride oral solution (a syrup) containing 10 mg in each 5 mL
Hydroxyzine pamoate capsules in 25 mg
There is also a hydroxyzine hydrochloride injection.
Hydroxyzine is given into a muscle by a healthcare professional.
It is never given into a vein or under the skin.
Hydroxyzine is not chemically related to benzodiazepines, phenothiazines, reserpine, or meprobamate.

narcotic (opioid) pain medicines
non-narcotic pain medicines
barbiturates

heart rhythm medicines such as quinidine, procainamide, amiodarone, and sotalol
certain antipsychotics such as ziprasidone, iloperidone, clozapine, quetiapine, and chlorpromazine
certain antidepressants such as citalopram and fluoxetine
certain antibiotics such as azithromycin, erythromycin, clarithromycin, gatifloxacin, and moxifloxacin
other medicines such as pentamidine, methadone, ondansetron, and droperidol
Hydroxyzine does not affect atropine or other belladonna alkaloids.
It is not known to interfere with digitalis.

candidates.subject: Hydroxyzine
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug may require changes in dosage based on the condition or factor specified in the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Hydroxyzine makes the effects of central nervous system depressants stronger.
If you take hydroxyzine with any of the following, your doctor may need to lower the dose of the other medicine.
narcotic (opioid) pain medicines
non-narcotic pain medicines
barbiturates
Hydroxyzine may increase the effects of meperidine and barbiturates when used before anesthesia.
Your doctor will adjust these doses for you individually.
Care is needed if you take other medicines.
These medicines can affect heart rhythm.
They do this by prolonging the QT interval.
These include:
heart rhythm medicines such as quinidine, procainamide, amiodarone, and sotalol
certain antipsychotics such as ziprasidone, iloperidone, clozapine, quetiapine, and chlorpromazine
certain antidepressants such as citalopram and fluoxetine
certain antibiotics such as azithromycin, erythromycin, clarithromycin, gatifloxacin, and moxifloxacin
other medicines such as pentamidine, methadone, ondansetron, and droperidol
Hydroxyzine does not affect atropine or other belladonna alkaloids.
It is not known to interfere with digitalis.

candidates.subject: Hydroxyzine
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Hydroxyzine is a prescription antihistamine.
It is used to treat anxiety and tension.
It is used to treat itching from allergic skin conditions.
It is used for sedation before and after general anesthesia.
Hydroxyzine comes in three oral forms:
Hydroxyzine hydrochloride (HCl) tablets in 10 mg, 25 mg, and 50 mg strengths
Hydroxyzine hydrochloride oral solution (a syrup) containing 10 mg in each 5 mL
Hydroxyzine pamoate capsules in 25 mg
There is also a hydroxyzine hydrochloride injection.
Hydroxyzine is given into a muscle by a healthcare professional.
It is never given into a vein or under the skin.
Hydroxyzine is not chemically related to benzodiazepines, phenothiazines, reserpine, or meprobamate.

candidates.subject: Hydroxyzine

candidates.evidence_text:
The most common side effects of hydroxyzine are drowsiness, dry mouth, and headache.
Drowsiness, dry mouth, and headache are usually mild and do not last long.
A skin rash is different.
If you develop a rash while taking hydroxyzine, stop taking hydroxyzine and call your doctor.
A rash can be the first sign of a serious reaction.
Common side effects:
Common hydroxyzine side effects include dry mouth, headache, and drowsiness.
The drowsiness is usually temporary.
It may go away after a few days of treatment.
It may go away when the dose is lowered.
Serious side effects:
Stop taking hydroxyzine and call your doctor right away if you develop a skin rash.
Stop taking hydroxyzine and call your doctor right away if a skin condition you are treating gets worse.
Stop taking hydroxyzine and call your doctor right away if you have any other sign of an allergic reaction.
In rare cases, hydroxyzine can cause a serious skin reaction called acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis (AGEP).

candidates.subject: Hydroxyzine
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug may cause the adverse effect or symptom specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Signs include fever together with many small, shallow, pus-filled spots appearing across large areas of swollen, red skin.
If you have had AGEP or another allergic reaction to hydroxyzine, you should also avoid cetirizine and levocetirizine.
This is because a similar reaction can happen with cetirizine and levocetirizine.
Hydroxyzine has also been linked to a heart rhythm problem called QT prolongation.
QT prolongation can lead to a serious irregular heartbeat known as Torsade de Pointes.
Other reported side effects include:
tremor or seizures (convulsions), which are rare and have usually happened at doses much higher than recommended
hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not there)
skin reactions including rash, hives, itching, and fixed drug eruptions, which are rashes that come back in the same spot each time the medicine is taken
allergic reaction
Serious breathing problems have not been reported at recommended doses.
If you are given hydroxyzine by injection, tell your healthcare provider straight away.

candidates.evidence_text:
Hydroxyzine makes the effects of central nervous system depressants stronger.
If you take hydroxyzine with any of the following, your doctor may need to lower the dose of the other medicine.
narcotic (opioid) pain medicines
non-narcotic pain medicines
barbiturates
Hydroxyzine may increase the effects of meperidine and barbiturates when used before anesthesia.
Your doctor will adjust these doses for you individually.
Care is needed if you take other medicines.
These medicines can affect heart rhythm.
They do this by prolonging the QT interval.
These include:
heart rhythm medicines such as quinidine, procainamide, amiodarone, and sotalol
certain antipsychotics such as ziprasidone, iloperidone, clozapine, quetiapine, and chlorpromazine
certain antidepressants such as citalopram and fluoxetine
certain antibiotics such as azithromycin, erythromycin, clarithromycin, gatifloxacin, and moxifloxacin
other medicines such as pentamidine, methadone, ondansetron, and droperidol
Hydroxyzine does not affect atropine or other belladonna alkaloids.
It is not known to interfere with digitalis.

Children 6 years and over: 50 to 100 mg a day, split into smaller doses

Children 6 years and over: 50 to 100 mg a day, split into smaller doses

Treatment can be started with an injection into a muscle.

Doctors usually start older adults on a low dose.

Your doctor will watch you closely.

candidates.evidence_text:
Hydroxyzine makes the effects of central nervous system depressants stronger.
If you take hydroxyzine with any of the following, your doctor may need to lower the dose of the other medicine.
narcotic (opioid) pain medicines
non-narcotic pain medicines
barbiturates

Your doctor will adjust these doses for you individually.
Care is needed if you take other medicines.
These medicines can affect heart rhythm.
They do this by prolonging the QT interval.
These include:
heart rhythm medicines such as quinidine, procainamide, amiodarone, and sotalol
certain antipsychotics such as ziprasidone, iloperidone, clozapine, quetiapine, and chlorpromazine
certain antidepressants such as citalopram and fluoxetine
certain antibiotics such as azithromycin, erythromycin, clarithromycin, gatifloxacin, and moxifloxacin
other medicines such as pentamidine, methadone, ondansetron, and droperidol
Hydroxyzine does not affect atropine or other belladonna alkaloids.
It is not known to interfere with digitalis.

Tell your doctor if you have anything that raises your risk of a heart rhythm problem called QT prolongation.
QT prolongation includes:
congenital long QT syndrome, a heart rhythm condition you are born with
a family history of long QT syndrome
a recent heart attack
heart failure that is not well controlled
a slow or irregular heartbeat (bradyarrhythmia)
other conditions that make heart rhythm problems more likely
Hydroxyzine should not be given to women who are breastfeeding.
It is not known whether hydroxyzine passes into breast milk.
Many medicines do.
The oral solution contains a small amount of alcohol, 0.5% by volume.
It is sweetened with sucrose.
Tell your doctor if either of these matters for you.

Take allopurinol exactly as prescribed by your doctor.
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Your doctor may occasionally change your dose.
Take the tablets with a full glass of water.
To reduce your risk of kidney stones, drink 8 to 10 full glasses of fluid every day.

Take allopurinol tablets after meals to help prevent stomach upset.
Allopurinol injection is injected into a vein by a healthcare provider.

You may need these tests even if you have no symptoms.
Your kidney and liver function may also need to be tested.
Your doctor may change your dose if your kidney function changes.

Keep taking Allopurinol as directed.
Your symptoms may not improve for up to 2 to 6 weeks.

Your doctor may occasionally change your dose.

Your doctor may recommend another gout medication to take with allopurinol.
Keep taking Allopurinol as directed.

candidates.evidence_text:
Allopurinol belongs to a class of medications called xanthine oxidase inhibitors.
Allopurinol works by reducing the production of uric acid in the body.
High levels of uric acid may cause gout attacks or kidney stones.
Allopurinol is used to treat gout.
Gout is a type of arthritis.
In gout, uric acid builds up in the joints.
Uric acid is a naturally occurring substance in the body.
The buildup of uric acid causes sudden attacks of redness, swelling, pain, and heat.
These attacks occur in one or more joints.
Allopurinol is used to prevent gout attacks.
It is not used to treat gout attacks once they occur.
Allopurinol does not need to be stopped during an acute flare.
Allopurinol is also used to treat high levels of uric acid.
The high levels of uric acid build up in the blood.
This buildup occurs as tumors break down.
This happens in people with certain types of cancer.
These people are being treated with chemotherapy medications.
Allopurinol is used to treat kidney stones.
The kidney stones have come back.
This treatment is for people with high levels of uric acid in their urine.

candidates.evidence_text:
Get emergency medical help if you have signs of an allergic reaction to allopurinol.
Signs of an allergic reaction to allopurinol include hives, difficult breathing, and swelling in your face or throat.
Get emergency medical help if you have a severe skin reaction.
Signs of a severe skin reaction include fever, sore throat, burning eyes, skin pain, and a red or purple skin rash with blistering and peeling.
Seek medical treatment if you have a serious drug reaction that can affect many parts of your body.
Symptoms may include skin rash, fever, swollen glands, muscle aches, severe weakness, unusual bruising, or yellowing of your skin or eyes.
Allopurinol may cause serious side effects.
Stop using Allopurinol and call your doctor at once if you have:
any skin rash, no matter how mild;
painful urination, blood in the urine;
inflammation of your blood vessels - numbness or tingling, skin rash, fever, headache, body aches, night sweats, weight loss, feeling or weak or tired;

This can make it easier for you to bleed from an injury or get sick from being around others who are ill.
Your blood may need to be tested often.
Visit your doctor regularly.
In rare cases, allopurinol may cause a severe allergic reaction.

Stop taking Allopurinol and call your doctor right away if you have blood in your urine.
Stop taking Allopurinol and call your doctor right away if you have burning in your eyes.
Stop taking Allopurinol and call your doctor right away if you have swelling in your face or throat.
Stop taking Allopurinol and call your doctor right away if you have skin redness.
Stop taking Allopurinol and call your doctor right away if you have a rash that spreads and causes blistering and peeling.
Avoid drinking alcohol.
Allopurinol can make your condition worse.
Allopurinol may impair your thinking or reactions.

candidates.object: drink 8 to 10 full glasses of fluid every day to reduce risk of kidney stones
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug should be taken or used in the manner specified by the object entity (for example with food or at a fixed time).
candidates.evidence_text:
Take allopurinol exactly as prescribed by your doctor.
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Your doctor may occasionally change your dose.
Take the tablets with a full glass of water.
To reduce your risk of kidney stones, drink 8 to 10 full glasses of fluid every day.
Do this unless your doctor tells you otherwise.
Take allopurinol tablets after meals to help prevent stomach upset.
Allopurinol injection is injected into a vein by a healthcare provider.
The injection is usually only used if you are unable to take medicine by mouth.
You may need frequent medical tests while using Allopurinol.
You may need these tests even if you have no symptoms.
Your kidney and liver function may also need to be tested.
Your doctor may change your dose if your kidney function changes.
You may have gout attacks when you first start taking allopurinol tablets.
Your doctor may recommend another gout medication to take with allopurinol.
Keep taking Allopurinol as directed.
Your symptoms may not improve for up to 2 to 6 weeks.

candidates.object: tell your doctor about all other medicines
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug should be taken or used in the manner specified by the object entity (for example with food or at a fixed time).
candidates.evidence_text:
Sometimes it is not safe to use certain medications at the same time.
Some drugs can affect your blood levels of other drugs you take.
This may increase side effects.
This may make the medications less effective.
Tell your doctor about all your other medicines, especially:
a stomach acid reducer such as omeprazole, Nexium, or Prilosec;
an antidepressant such as citalopram, fluoxetine, sertraline, Cymbalta, Effexor, Lexapro, Pristiq, or Prozac;
rifampin;
a blood thinner --warfarin, Coumadin, Jantoven; or
NSAIDs (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs) --aspirin, ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), celecoxib, diclofenac, indomethacin, meloxicam, and others.
This list is not complete.
Other drugs may affect clopidogrel.
These other drugs include prescription and over-the-counter medicines.
These other drugs also include vitamins and herbal products.
Not all possible drug interactions are listed here.

candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug may require changes in dosage based on the condition or factor specified in the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Usual Adult Dose for Acute Coronary Syndrome:
Unstable Angina (UA)/Non-ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (NSTEMI) has a loading dose of 300 mg orally once.
The maintenance dose is 75 mg orally once a day.
The duration of therapy is optimal unknown.
ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI) has an optional loading dose of 300 mg orally once.
The maintenance dose is 75 mg orally once a day, with or without thrombolytics.
The optimal duration of therapy is unknown.
Comments: -Administer Clopidogrel in combination with aspirin 75 mg to 325 mg orally once a day.
The benefit of Clopidogrel is unknown.
This applies to patients who undergo primary percutaneous coronary intervention.
Uses include prevention of atherothrombotic events.
This applies to patients with non-ST-segment elevation acute coronary syndrome.
This includes patients with UA.
This includes patients with NSTEMI.
This includes those who are to be managed medically.
This includes those who are to be managed with coronary revascularization.
This also applies to patients with STEMI.
Usual Adult Dose for Ischemic Stroke:

candidates.subject: clopidogrel
candidates.object: read all medication guides or instruction sheets
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug should be taken or used in the manner specified by the object entity (for example with food or at a fixed time).
candidates.evidence_text:
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Use these medicines exactly as directed.
Clopidogrel can be taken with or without food.
Clopidogrel is sometimes taken together with aspirin.
Take aspirin only if your doctor tells you to.
Clopidogrel keeps your blood from coagulating (clotting).
It can make it easier for you to bleed, even from a minor injury.
Contact your doctor or seek emergency medical attention if you have any bleeding that will not stop.
You may need to stop using clopidogrel for a short time before a surgery, medical procedure, or dental work.
Any healthcare provider who treats you should know that you are taking clopidogrel.
Do not stop taking clopidogrel without first talking to your doctor, even if you have signs of bleeding.
Stopping the medicine could increase your risk of a heart attack or stroke.
Store at room temperature away from moisture and heat.

candidates.evidence_text:
Ergocalciferol is vitamin D2.
Vitamin D helps your body absorb calcium.
Ergocalciferol is used to treat hypoparathyroidism (decreased functioning of the parathyroid glands).
Ergocalciferol is also used to treat rickets.
Rickets is the softening of the bones caused by vitamin D deficiency.
Ergocalciferol is also used to treat low levels of phosphate in the blood.
Low levels of phosphate in the blood are known as hypophosphatemia.
Ergocalciferol may also be used for purposes not listed in this medication guide.

candidates.evidence_text:
You should not take ergocalciferol if you have had an allergic reaction to vitamin D, or if you have:
high levels of vitamin D in your body (hypervitaminosis D);
high levels of calcium in your blood (hypercalcemia); or
any condition that makes it hard for your body to absorb nutrients from food (malabsorption).
Tell your doctor if you have ever had:
heart disease;
kidney disease; or
an electrolyte imbalance.
Certain forms of ergocalciferol may contain ingredients you should know about.
These ingredients include peanut or soybean oil, sugar, aspartame (phenylalanine), or certain food dyes.
Ask a doctor before using ergocalciferol if you have allergies, diabetes, or phenylketonuria (PKU).
Too much vitamin D could harm an unborn baby.
Your dose needs may be different during pregnancy.
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or if you become pregnant while taking ergocalciferol.
Ergocalciferol can pass into breast milk.
It may cause side effects in the nursing baby.
Tell your doctor if you are breast-feeding.
Do not give ergocalciferol to a child without medical advice.

candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug carries the warning specified by the object entity regarding use during pregnancy or while breastfeeding.
candidates.evidence_text:
You should not take ergocalciferol if you have had an allergic reaction to vitamin D, or if you have:
high levels of vitamin D in your body (hypervitaminosis D);
high levels of calcium in your blood (hypercalcemia); or
any condition that makes it hard for your body to absorb nutrients from food (malabsorption).
Tell your doctor if you have ever had:
heart disease;
kidney disease; or
an electrolyte imbalance.
Certain forms of ergocalciferol may contain ingredients you should know about.
These ingredients include peanut or soybean oil, sugar, aspartame (phenylalanine), or certain food dyes.
Ask a doctor before using ergocalciferol if you have allergies, diabetes, or phenylketonuria (PKU).
Too much vitamin D could harm an unborn baby.
Your dose needs may be different during pregnancy.
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or if you become pregnant while taking ergocalciferol.
Ergocalciferol can pass into breast milk.
It may cause side effects in the nursing baby.
Tell your doctor if you are breast-feeding.
Do not give ergocalciferol to a child without medical advice.

chest pain, feeling short of breath;
growth problems (in a child taking ergocalciferol); or
early signs of vitamin D overdose --weakness, metallic taste in your mouth, weight loss, muscle or bone pain, constipation, nausea, and vomiting.

chest pain, feeling short of breath;
growth problems (in a child taking ergocalciferol); or
early signs of vitamin D overdose --weakness, metallic taste in your mouth, weight loss, muscle or bone pain, constipation, nausea, and vomiting.
Less serious side effects may be more likely.

Call your doctor for medical advice about side effects.

candidates.evidence_text:
You should not take ergocalciferol if you have had an allergic reaction to vitamin D, or if you have:
high levels of vitamin D in your body (hypervitaminosis D);
high levels of calcium in your blood (hypercalcemia); or
any condition that makes it hard for your body to absorb nutrients from food (malabsorption).
Tell your doctor if you have ever had:
heart disease;
kidney disease; or
an electrolyte imbalance.
Certain forms of ergocalciferol may contain ingredients you should know about.
These ingredients include peanut or soybean oil, sugar, aspartame (phenylalanine), or certain food dyes.
Ask a doctor before using ergocalciferol if you have allergies, diabetes, or phenylketonuria (PKU).
Too much vitamin D could harm an unborn baby.
Your dose needs may be different during pregnancy.
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or if you become pregnant while taking ergocalciferol.
Ergocalciferol can pass into breast milk.
It may cause side effects in the nursing baby.
Tell your doctor if you are breast-feeding.
Do not give ergocalciferol to a child without medical advice.

You should also not drink alcohol while taking either of these medications because it can make these side effects worse.

gt.section_title: What other drugs will affect ondansetron?
gt.evidence_text: Ondansetron can cause a serious heart problem, especially if you use certain medicines at the same time, including antibiotics, antidepressants, heart rhythm medicine, antipsychotic medicines, and medicines to treat cancer, malaria, HIV or AIDS. Tell your doctor about all medicines you use, and those you start or stop using during your treatment with ondansetron.

candidates.subject: Ondansetron
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug may cause the serious or potentially dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity that requires medical attention.
candidates.evidence_text:
Ondansetron can cause a serious heart problem.
This risk is especially high if you use certain medicines at the same time.
These medicines include antibiotics, antidepressants, heart rhythm medicine, antipsychotic medicines, and medicines to treat cancer, malaria, HIV or AIDS.
Tell your doctor about all medicines you use, and those you start or stop using during your treatment with ondansetron.
Taking ondansetron while using certain other medicines can cause high levels of serotonin to build up in your body.
This condition is called "serotonin syndrome."
Serotonin syndrome can be fatal.
Tell your doctor if you also use:
medicine to treat depression;
medicine to treat a psychiatric disorder;
a narcotic (opioid) medication; or
medicine to prevent nausea and vomiting.
This list is not complete and many other drugs can interact with ondansetron.
List includes prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.
Give a list of all your medicines to any healthcare provider who treats you.

candidates.subject: Ondansetron
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug may cause the serious or potentially dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity that requires medical attention.
candidates.evidence_text:
You should not use ondansetron if you are also using apomorphine (Apokyn).
You should not use ondansetron if you are allergic to ondansetron.

candidates.evidence_text:
Ondansetron can cause a serious heart problem.
This risk is especially high if you use certain medicines at the same time.
These medicines include antibiotics, antidepressants, heart rhythm medicine, antipsychotic medicines, and medicines to treat cancer, malaria, HIV or AIDS.
Tell your doctor about all medicines you use, and those you start or stop using during your treatment with ondansetron.
Taking ondansetron while using certain other medicines can cause high levels of serotonin to build up in your body.
This condition is called "serotonin syndrome."
Serotonin syndrome can be fatal.
Tell your doctor if you also use:
medicine to treat depression;
medicine to treat a psychiatric disorder;
a narcotic (opioid) medication; or
medicine to prevent nausea and vomiting.
This list is not complete and many other drugs can interact with ondansetron.
List includes prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, and herbal products.
Give a list of all your medicines to any healthcare provider who treats you.

candidates.subject: Cyclobenzaprine
candidates.relation_definition: The subject drug decreases or lessens the condition or effect specified by the object entity.
candidates.evidence_text:
Cyclobenzaprine is a prescription muscle relaxant.
It is used short-term to relieve muscle spasms.
The spasms are caused by sprains, strains, and injuries.
These include low back and neck pain.
Cyclobenzaprine is used together with rest and physical therapy.
This combination helps relieve pain, tenderness, and limited movement.
These symptoms are caused by muscle spasm.
1,2
Cyclobenzaprine is also used to treat fibromyalgia in adults.
Cyclobenzaprine can help reduce pain.
For fibromyalgia, Cyclobenzaprine is taken as a sublingual (under the tongue) tablet at bedtime under the brand name Tonmya.
In clinical trials, Tonmya significantly reduced fibromyalgia pain compared with placebo over 14 weeks.
Close to half of treated patients achieved at least a 30% improvement in pain.
3
The Flexeril brand has been discontinued.
Cyclobenzaprine is available as generic tablets.
Cyclobenzaprine is also available as the brand-name products Amrix (extended-release capsules) and Fexmid.
2,4

candidates.evidence_text:
Cyclobenzaprine works by reducing the nerve signals in the brain.
These signals drive muscle tone and spasm.
This reduction allows tight, overactive muscles to relax.
Cyclobenzaprine acts within the central nervous system.
It acts primarily at the level of the brain stem.
It does not act on the muscles themselves.
It does not act at the junction between nerves and muscle.
Cyclobenzaprine works through the nervous system in this way.
Cyclobenzaprine will not relieve muscle spasm caused by central nervous system disease.
Examples of central nervous system disease include cerebral palsy or spinal cord disease.
1,2
The way cyclobenzaprine works in fibromyalgia is not known.
Laboratory studies show Cyclobenzaprine blocks several receptor types.
These receptor types include serotonin (5-HT2A), histamine, and muscarinic receptors.
3
Cyclobenzaprine is chemically related to tricyclic antidepressants such as amitriptyline.
This relationship explains several of Cyclobenzaprine's side effects.
These side effects include drowsiness and dry mouth.

Cyclobenzaprine dose for muscle spasm:
Cyclobenzaprine is usually taken for up to 2 or 3 weeks for muscle spasm.
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Your doctor may occasionally change your dose.
Immediate-release tablets are taken three times a day.
Extended-release capsules are taken once daily, at about the same time each day.
Swallow the capsules whole.
You can open the capsule if you have difficulty swallowing them.
Sprinkle the contents onto a tablespoon of applesauce.
Swallow the mixture right away.
Do not chew the mixture.
Follow your doctor's dosing instructions very carefully.
Cyclobenzaprine for fibromyalgia:
Tonmya is taken once daily at bedtime, after brushing your teeth.
Drink a few sips of water first so your mouth is moist.
Place the tablet(s) under your tongue until dissolved.
Do not swallow whole, cut, crush, or chew.
Avoid eating or drinking for at least 15 minutes afterward.
Avoid hot, cold, or acidic drinks until morning.
Avoid talking for about 5 minutes after dosing.

These include low back and neck pain.
Cyclobenzaprine is used together with rest and physical therapy.
This combination helps relieve pain, tenderness, and limited movement.
These symptoms are caused by muscle spasm.
1,2

Close to half of treated patients achieved at least a 30% improvement in pain.

Cyclobenzaprine is also available as the brand-name products Amrix (extended-release capsules) and Fexmid.

gt.section_title: What is the usual spironolactone dosage?
gt.evidence_text:
Spironolactone dosage for heart failure:
Treatment starts at spironolactone 25 mg once a day, provided your potassium level is 5.0 mEq/L or lower and your kidney function (eGFR) is above 50. If you tolerate that, the dose may go up to 50 mg once a day. If your potassium rises too high, the dose may drop to 25 mg every other day. If your eGFR is between 30 and 50, your doctor may start you at 25 mg every other day because of the higher risk of high potassium.

potassium supplements and potassium-containing salt substitutes, which are usually stopped when spironolactone is started for heart failure;
Spironolactone slows how fast your kidneys clear spironolactone.
